procnotices.notice_text:
République de Côte d’Ivoire

                                     --------------------------------

                          MINISTERE DU PLAN ET DU DEVELOPPEMENT

                              -------------------------------

        PROJET D’HARMONISATION ET D’AMELIORATION DES STATISTIQUES

                                 ------------------------------

Financement Groupe de la Banque mondiale : Crédits IDA n° 65750 & 78840-CI

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET N° CI-INS COTE D'IVOIRE-565978-CS-INDV

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET D’AUDIT POUR L’AUDIT COMPTABLE ET FINANCIER DU PROJET D’HARMONISATION ET D’AMELIORATION DES STATISTIQUES AU TITRE DE L’EXERCICE 2026 ET DE L’AUDIT DE CLOTURE DU PROJET

 

           I. CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

La République de Côte d’Ivoire bénéficie d’un crédit de 45 millions USD dans le cadre d’un financement global de 379 millions USD de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) pour contribuer à l’harmonisation et au renforcement des systèmes statistiques dans sept pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest (Burkina Faso, Cap Vert, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Libéria, Sierra Leone et Togo).

Le projet vise à contribuer à une amélioration et une harmonisation des statistiques économiques et sociales dans la sous-région ouest-africaine.

Les activités du projet sont structurées sous trois composantes que sont :

1)       une composante régionale pour produire des outils harmonisés, collecter un ensemble de statistiques sociales, économiques et administratives de base tout en améliorant leur qualité, diffuser et faciliter l'utilisation des données, ainsi qu’améliorer l’environnement institutionnel au niveau de la gestion et de la capacité des ressources humaines ;

2)       une composante propre à chaque pays pour remédier aux lacunes qui ne sont pas nécessairement communes à tous les pays mais qui permettront aux Systèmes Statistiques Nationaux de tirer parti des activités régionales, par exemple en répondant aux besoins en matière d’infrastructures et de logiciels ; et

3)       une composante de gestion de projet pour surveiller et superviser les activités 1 et 2.

Le cadre institutionnel et organisationnel du Projet prévoit les organes suivants :

-         (i) un Comité de pilotage du Projet (CPP) ;

-         (ii) un Comité Technique ;

-         (iii) une Unité de Coordination du Projet (UCP) ayant en charge la gestion des ressources du projet et qui assurera la coordination globale des aspects administratifs et fiduciaires du projet à travers ses différentes composantes.

-         (iv) une Cellule de points focaux qui sont les responsables des activités représentant les structures du Projet

Le présent avis à manifestation d’intérêt est élaboré en vue de la sélection d’un cabinet d’audit pour la réalisation de l’audit comptable et financier au titre de l’exercice 2026 et de l’audit de clôture du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques (PHAS).

            II. OBJECTIFS DE LA MISSION

L’objectif de l’audit comptable et financier est de :

  • permettre d’exprimer une opinion professionnelle et indépendante sur la situation financière du Projet au titre du prêt à la fin de chaque exercice comptable y compris sur le compte désigné et les relevés de dépenses ;
  • s’assurer que les ressources mises à la disposition du Projet sont utilisées aux fins pour lesquelles elles ont été octroyées en vue de l’atteinte de l’Objectif de Développement du Projet ;
  • s’assurer que les états financiers, qui sont établis par le Projet sont élaborés de manière à rendre compte de manière sincère des transactions financières du Projet ;
  • procéder à l’examen et à l’évaluation du dispositif de contrôle interne adéquat ainsi qu’une documentation acceptable des transactions.

L’audit sera réalisé conformément aux Normes Internationales d’Audit (International Standard of Auditing) définies par l’International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) et comprendra tous les tests et les contrôles jugés nécessaires par l’Auditeur eu égard aux circonstances.

         III. RESULTATS ATTENDUS

  • Les résultats attendus de la mission sont :
  • réalisation de l’audit comptable et financier au titre de l’exercice 2026 ;
  • réalisation de l’audit de clôture du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques

            IV. DUREE DE LA MISSION

La mission d’audit sera exécutée sur une durée maximum de quarante-cinq (45) jours calendaires (y compris la remise du rapport final d’audit) à compter de la date de démarrage indiquée dans l’Ordre de Service qui sera notifié au consultant pour l’exercice concerné.

            V. TACHES ET RESPONSABILITES DU CABINET

L’auditeur s’assurera que :

  • toutes les ressources de la Banque Mondiale ont été employées conformément aux dispositions de l’Accord de financement dans un souci d’économie et d’efficience, et uniquement aux fins pour lesquelles elles ont été fournies ;
  • les fonds de contrepartie nationale (budget de l’Etat) ont été obtenus et employés conformément aux dispositions des accords de financement applicables, dans un souci d’économie et d’efficience, et uniquement aux fins pour lesquelles ils ont été fournis ;
  • les acquisitions des biens et services financés ont fait l’objet de marchés passés conformément aux dispositions des accords de financement applicables fondés sur les procédures de passation de marché de la Banque Mondiale et ont été proprement enregistrés dans les livres comptables ;
  • tous les dossiers, comptes et écritures nécessaires ont été tenus au titre des différentes opérations relatives au Projet (y compris les dépenses couvertes par des relevés de dépenses ou des rapports de suivi financier) ;
  • les Comptes Désignés sont gérés eu égard aux dispositions de l’accord de financement du Projet ;
  • traitement fiscal applicable aux rémunérations versées au personnel contractuel et aux consultants de l’Unité de Gestion du projet et autres consultants individuels ;
  • la gestion des fonds de contrepartie ou tout autre fonds de l’Etat décaissé dans le cadre de ce projet est conforme aux dispositions applicables au projet notamment le Décret 475 (Instruction 192 révisée) relatif aux modalités de gestion des projets financés par les PTFs et l’accord de financement.
  • Etc.

Les termes de référence peuvent être retirés en faisant une demande écrite à l’adresse : t.ourega@stat.plan.gouv.ci avec en copie phas@stat.plan.gouv.ci

          VI. PROFIL DU CABINET

Le Consultant doit être un Cabinet d’Audit et d’Expertise Comptable indépendant, faisant profession habituelle de réviser les comptes, régulièrement inscrit au Tableau d’un Ordre des Experts-Comptables reconnu au plan international par l’IFAC ou la FIDEF.

Il doit :

  • justifier d’au moins 5 ans d’expériences dans le domaine de l’audit comptable et financier des projets de développement ;
  • avoir audité les états financiers annuels d’au moins dix (10) projets financés par les Partenaires Techniques et Financiers (PTFs) ;
  • avoir réalisé l’audit des comptes d’au moins cinq (05) projets financés par la Banque mondiale ;
  • avoir une connaissance suffisante des dispositions administratives et réglementaires en Côte d’Ivoire ;
  • avoir une connaissance suffisante des normes internationales en matière d’audit financier et comptable.

N.B : L’expérience du cabinet est évaluée à partir des Attestations de Bonne Exécution (ABE) accompagnées des fiches projets.

 VII. CONSTITUTION ET DEPOT DES MANIFESTATION D’INTERETS

Les manifestations d’intérêt élaborées exclusivement en français, devront comprendre :

  1. une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt précisant l’objet de la manifestation d’intérêt adressée au Coordonnateur National du PHAS ;
  2. une fiche fournissant des informations sur la dénomination de la firme, sa nature juridique, sa création, etc. ;
  3. la preuve d’inscription du cabinet au tableau d’un Ordre des Experts-Comptables reconnu au plan international par l’IFAC ou la FIDEF ;
  4. la garantie de l’application des Normes International d’Audit ;
  5. des fiches de projet décrivant toutes les références relatives aux missions d’audit comptables et financiers (montant, date, durée, lieu, description des tâches réalisées, nature du client).

Les manifestations d’intérêts en français seront transmises physiquement ou électroniquement aux adresses ci-dessous indiquées au plus tard le jeudi 24/09/2026, à 10 heures GMT en cinq (05) exemplaires (01 original et 04 copies) sous plis fermés avec la mention : « Recrutement d’un cabinet d’audit pour l’audit comptable et financier du Projet d’Harmonisation et d’Amélioration des Statistiques (PHAS) au titre de l’exercice 2026 et de l’audit de clôture du projet » ou par voie électronique : t.ourega@stat.plan.gouv.ci avec en copie phas@stat.plan.gouv.ci

Unité de Coordination du PHAS sise à Abidjan, Cocody Angré 7ème Tranche en face du projet filets sociaux productifs. Téléphone : (+225) 07 11 11 11 23

 

             VIII. PROCEDURE DE SELECTION

La procédure de recrutement de la firme sera conduite conformément à la méthode de Sélection au Moindre Coût (SMC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés de la Banque mondiale de juillet 2016, révisé en septembre 2025.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

COUNTRY: KYRGYZ REPUBLIC

NAME OF PROJECT: "Kyrgyz Renewable Energy Development Project" (KRED) – Phase 1

Credit No.: IDA 7370-KG

Assignment Title: Consulting services for the preparation of preliminary design, tender documentation and evaluation of bids in the selection of a Contractor for the construction of the 110 kV overhead line between the Lower Tar HPP and the "Kara-Kulja" Substation

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan) KG/KRED/CS/2026/CQS-01

The Kyrgyz Republic has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Kyrgyz Renewable Energy Development Project (KRED) – Phase 1 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the preparation of the preliminary design and tender documentation, and support in the evaluation of bids for the construction of the 110 kV overhead transmission line between the Lower Tar HPP and the Kara-Kulja Substation.

Under Component 1 of the KRED Project, a new 110 kV overhead transmission line of approximately 18 km is envisaged to connect the 19 MW Lower Tar Small HPP, located in Kara-Kulja District, Osh Region, to the existing 110 kV Kara-Kulja Substation. The transmission line is expected to be constructed under a Design, Supply and Installation contract based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Document.

The objective of the assignment is to engage a consulting firm to prepare the preliminary design of the 110 kV overhead transmission line, prepare the complete tender package based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Document, and provide support during the selection of the Contractor. The Consultant will also coordinate interfaces with the Kara-Kulja Substation and the 110 kV switchyard of the Lower Tar HPP, obtain the technical connection conditions from OJSC “National Electric Grid of Kyrgyzstan” (NEGK), support the approval of the transmission line route, and assist with responses to bidders’ queries, bid evaluation and contract award.

The services are expected to commence in Q4 2026. Approximately five (5) months are envisaged for completion of the preliminary design and tender documentation. The contract will be lump sum.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be downloaded from the link below:

Terms of Reference (in English) https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B2AbYUWYXekAKe-XerXJL7kD3XjxcA2k/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=112497473623936364216&rtpof=true&sd=true

Terms of Reference (in Russian) https://docs.google.com/document/d/1L9v5GAzL9BtspL4Nn5dFQCLmJwJ8CtHi/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=112497473623936364216&rtpof=true&sd=true

The Ministry of Energy (MoE) now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

1. At least 10 years of consulting experience in the power sector, with the design of overhead transmission lines and substations of 110 kV and above as one of the core areas of activity.

2. At least three (3) similar assignments on the design of overhead transmission lines of 110 kV and above and/or substations, including the preparation of bills of quantities and specifications of equipment and materials, over the last 10 years. Experience in similar assignments in mountainous and seismic conditions and/or in Central Asia and the CIS will be considered an advantage.

3. Experience in the preparation of tender documentation and provision of support during the tendering process for infrastructure projects in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations and/or the procurement rules of other International Financial Institutions (IFIs).

Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" September 2023 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications (type of association shall be clearly indicated in the proposal). The Consultants may submit their Expressions of Interest as individual firms or associate in the form of joint venture or sub-consultancy. However, the qualification of the sub-consultant will not be evaluated when forming the shortlist. In case of joint venture, all the members of the joint venture should individually meet shortlisting criteria and shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant's Qualifications Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained using the e-mail: kred.pmo@gmail.com

Expressions of Interest should be submitted, in English, electronically to kred.pmo@gmail.com by September 10, 2026 16h00 Bishkek time (GMT+6).

----------

THE COORDINATION UNIT

----------

 

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

N°001/AMI/MINEPAT/PSRDREN/PACRI-MDK/SPM  DU 03 SEPTEMBRE 2026

POUR LA MISE EN ŒUVRE DE LA STRATEGIE POUR LA PROMOTION DE L’ENTREPRENEURIAT AGRICOLE FEMININ DANS LES ARRONDISSEMENTS DE MAKARY, LOGONE BIRNI ET KOUSSERI POUR LE PROJET D’AMÉLIORATION DE LA CONNECTIVITÉ, LA RÉSILIENCE ET L’INCLUSION LE LONG DU CORRIDOR MORA - DABANGA - KOUSSERI (PACRI-MDK)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

PAYS : Cameroun

 

PROJET : Projet pour l’Amélioration de la Connectivité, la Résilience et l’Inclusion le long du corridor routier Mora-Dabanga-Kousséri dans la Région de l’Extrême-Nord « PACRI-MDK »

 

FINANCEMENT : Crédit IDA N° 73520-CM / N°73510-CM / N°2090-CM

 

TITRE DE LA MISSION : mise en œuvre de la stratégie pour la promotion de l’entrepreneuriat agricole féminin dans les arrondissements de Makary, Logone birni et Kousseri pour le Projet d’Amélioration de la Connectivité et de la Résilience et de l’Inclusion le long du corridor routier Mora-Dabanga-Kousseri (PACRI-MDK) ».

 

Numéro de référence : CM-MINEPAT-567042-CS-QCBS

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Cameroun à travers le Ministère de l’Economie, de la Planification et de l’Aménagement du Territoire, a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet pour l’Amélioration de la Connectivité, la Résilience et l’Inclusion le long de l’axe routier Mora-Dabanga-Kousseri (PACRI-MDK) et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit à des services de consultant.
  2. Les services de consultant (“les Services”) comprennent pour les groupes de femmes : le ciblage, la structuration, le renforcement de capacité et Coaching ; le développement économique, l’appui aux business plans et l’accès au financement; la structuration organisationnelle, la gouvernance et la pérennisation; le suivi-évaluation, le reporting et la capitalisation. Ces services se dérouleront sur 30 mois. Les Termes de Référence peuvent être retirés auprès de l’Unité de Coordination du PACRI-MDK à Maroua à Pitoaré à côté du club KALIAO et à Yaoundé au bâtiment annexe du MINEPAT entre le carrefour Lissouck et le camp YEYAP.
  3.  Le Coordonnateur du Programme Spécial de Reconstruction et de Développement de la Région de l’Extrême Nord invite dès à présent les firmes/ONG/OSC admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant:
  • de l’existence égale: copie de l’acte de création (registre de commerce, attestation d’immatriculation, …), document justifiant que le soumissionnaire n’a pas de dette fiscale ;
  • qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services. Les critères de sélection d’une liste restreinte sont les suivants : expérience générale au cours des dix dernières années et expériences similaires (l'entrepreneuriat féminin, l'autonomisation économique des femmes ou l'accompagnement de femmes et de groupements féminins) au cours des dix dernières années. NB : Le Consultant devra obligatoirement fournir dans son offre pour chaque référence, les justificatifs de ses références en termes de contrat déjà réalisés avec succès (1ere page, 2e page ou toute page du contrat permettant d’avoir une meilleure compréhension de l’activité, page de signature des contrats, PV de recette technique ou attestation de bonne fin). Les références réalisées en zone rurale du septentrion du Cameroun constitueront des atouts.
  1. La liste restreinte comprendra cinq consultants au moins et huit consultants au plus.
  2. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.13, 3.15 et 3.16 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, révisé en septembre 2025 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés»), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.
  3. Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.
  4. Les Consultants seront sélectionnés conformément aux dispositions de la Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement sous-décrite, sur la base du nombre total de projets pertinents et d’expérience présentés et justifiés pour les critères sus référencés.
  5. Des informations supplémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau 07h30 à 15h30.
  6. Les manifestations d’intérêt doivent être fournies par écrit ou par mail à l’adresse ci-dessous aux heures ouvrables ou par email (fanch2010@yahoo.fr). Les termes de référence de cette mission sont disponibles et peuvent être retirés à L’Unité de Coordination du Programme Spécial de Reconstruction et du Développement de la Région de l’Extrême Nord ou envoyés par e-mail aux consultants intéressés, à leur demande; au plus tard quatorze (14) jours après publication à 15h30.

 

« Appel à Manifestation d’Intérêt pour la mise en œuvre de la stratégie pour la promotion de l’entrepreneuriat agricole féminin dans les arrondissements du Makary, Logone birni et Kousseri pour le Projet d’Amélioration de la Connectivité et de la Résilience et de l’Inclusion le long du corridor routier Mora-Dabanga-Kousseri (PACRI-MDK) »

 

A l’Unité de Coordination du Programme Spécial de Reconstruction et du Développement de la Région de l’Extrême Nord

 A Yaoundé, au bâtiment annexe du MINEPAT sis à MESSA au Carrefour LISSOUCK en allant vers le camp YEYAP, au bureau du Spécialiste en Passation de Marchés du PACRI-MDK.

 

 

Yaoundé, le 03 septembre 2026

  Le COORDONNATEUR DU PSRDREN

MINISTRY OF LANDS, PUBLIC WORKS, HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

STATE DEPARTMENT FOR HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Consulting Services – Firm Selection

_______________________________________________________________________­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­

COUNTRY:                                    The Republic of Kenya

PROJECT TITLE:                       Second Kenya Urban Support Program (KUSP II)

PROJECT ID:                                P177048                                                       

CREDIT NO.:                               7349-KE; 7350-KE; IDA Grant Number E208-KE

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:             Consulting Services for the Preparation of Municipal Investment Opportunity Packages and Investment Readiness Support for Kisumu, Eldoret, Meru, Ruiru and Kakuma Municipalities in Kenya

CONTRACT NO.:                        KE-MOTI-566726-CS-QCBS

1.The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank (the Bank) towards the cost of the Second Kenya Urban Support Program (KUSP II) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2.The aim of the consulting services (“the Services”) is to prepare Municipal Investment Opportunity Packages for each municipality that can attract private sector participation and improve urban service delivery and local economic development. The Consulting Services is expected to be for a period of eight (8) calendar months from the date of contract commencement.

3.The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR’s) for the assignment can be found at the following websites – www.housingandurban.go.ke and www.kusp.go.ke or can be obtained at the address given below;

4.The State Department for Housing and Urban Development (the Client) in the Ministry of Lands, Public Works, Housing and Urban Development – now invites eligible Consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services; Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and experience to perform the services (attach evidence). The shortlisting criteria are:

a. Core business and years in business: The firm shall be duly registered/incorporated as a consulting firm with core business in the fields of municipal and urban infrastructure advisory, infrastructure finance, investment facilitation, project preparation, and/or private sector participation in urban development and service delivery. The firm shall demonstrate experience in undertaking municipal investment diagnostics, identifying and prioritizing investment opportunities, conducting pre-feasibility assessments, preparing investment opportunity packages, and strengthening institutional investment readiness for a minimum period of fifteen (15) years.

b. Must have relevant experience: The firm shall demonstrate having successfully executed and completed at least two (2) assignments of similar nature, scope, and complexity within the last ten (10) years. The assignments should demonstrate experience in: (i) undertaking municipal or urban economic and investment diagnostics; (ii) identifying and prioritizing viable investment opportunities in urban infrastructure and service delivery; (iii) conducting technical, financial, institutional, environmental, and social pre-feasibility assessments; (iv) preparing investment opportunity packages; and (v) supporting investment readiness, structured private sector engagement, or investment facilitation for counties, or urban areas.

Details of similar assignments—including the name and address of the client, scope of services, contract value, implementation period, and key outputs/deliverables—should be provided in the submitted Expression of Interest (EOI), together with a clear description of the relevance of the assignments to the scope of this consultancy.

c. Technical and managerial capability of the firm: The firm shall demonstrate as having the requisite technical and managerial capacity to undertake the assignment in the submitted company profile(s).

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

5. The attention of Consultants’ is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and Revised Fourth Edition November 2020 (Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6.The Consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Quality Cost Based Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

7. Further information can be obtained at the address given below from 0900hrs to 1700hrs East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300hrs-1400hrs) and public holidays.

8. Expression of interest should be delivered by Tuesday 6th October 2026 at 1000hrs EAT using one of the following modalities:

a. Deposit in the Tender Box located on 6th Floor, Ardhi House in Nairobi, Kenya;

b. Send via email to; kusp2proc@housingandurban.go.ke .

9. Expressions of Interest must be delivered in written form to either the tender box located at located on 6th Floor, Ardhi House in Nairobi, Kenya or e-mail: kusp2proc@housingandurban.go.ke  and clearly marked with the Assignment Title and Contract Number as indicated above and addressed to:

procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIQUE DU SENEGAL

Un Peuple – Un But – Une Foi

------------------

MINISTERE DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT ET DE LA TRANSITION ECOLOGIQUE (METE)

-------------------

PROJET DE GESTION DES RESSOURCES NATURELLES AU SENEGAL (SENRM)

 

 

Travaux de construction et d’aménagement de la piste Oubadji - Dalaba dans le Parc National de Niokolo Koba (P.N.N.K)

_______________________________

 

Pays : Sénégal

Projet : Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM/METE)

 Titre du Marché :  Travaux de construction et d’aménagement de la piste Oubadji-Dalaba dans le Parc national du Niokolo-Koba (PNNK)

Crédit No : 71890

Appel d’Offres No : T_SENRM/MEDDTE_013 (Réf. SYGMAP : T_SENRM_004)

 

1.     L’Etat du Sénégal a obtenu un crédit de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre du marché relatif aux Travaux de construction et d’aménagement de la piste Oubadji-Dalaba du dans le Parc National du Niokolo-Koba (PNNK).

2.       Le Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM METE) invite, par la présente, les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles à soumettre des Offres sous pli fermé, pour la réalisation des Travaux de construction et d’aménagement de la piste Oubadji – Dalaba dans le Parc National de Niokolo Koba PNNK pour une durée de cinq (05) mois.

3.       La passation de marchés sera conduite par passation de marchés au niveau national en utilisant un Document d’Appel d’Offres (DAO) tel que défini dans les « Règles des Passation de Marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs de FPI de septembre 2025 », et est ouverte à tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles.

4.       Les soumissionnaires doivent remplir les conditions de qualifications ci-après :

-        Justifier l’exécution d’au moins un marché similaire d’un montant de neuf cent vingt millions neuf cent trente-quatre mille (920 934 000) FCFA au cours des cinq (05) dernières années (2021 à 2025) ;

-    Produire une attestation de capacité financière ou une ligne de crédits d’un montant de trois cent quatre-vingt-trois millions sept cent vingt-deux mille (383 722 000) FCFA, délivré par un organisme bancaire ou une compagnie de cautionnement agréé par le Ministère en charge des finances ou par une institution bancaire ou de cautionnement étrangère disposant d’un correspondant local agréé par le Ministère en charge des finances.

-      Avoir un chiffre d’affaires annuel moyen d’au moins un milliard sept cent vingt-six millions (1.726.000.000) F CFA, au cours des cinq (05) dernières années (2021 à 2025). Produire les états financiers certifiés par un expert-comptable agréé par l’ONECCA ou un organisme assimilé au cours des cinq dernières années (2021 à 2025).

 Pour les détails, veuillez consulter l’annexe A aux données particulières du dossier d’appel d’offres.

5.  Les Soumissionnaires intéressés de pays éligibles peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires auprès de la Spécialiste de Passation des Marchés du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM/METE) ; adresse électronique : passationdemarches.senrmmeddte@gmail.com  et examiner le Document d’Appel d’Offres durant les heures de bureau de 9 :00 à 17 :00 heures à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous : Projet SENRM, 7ème étage de l’Immeuble Magnolia, VDN, Sud foire, lot N°30 SIPRES, Dakar.

6.       Le Document d’Appel d’Offres en Français peut être acheté par tous les Soumissionnaires de pays éligibles en formulant une demande écrite à la Coordonnatrice du Projet et déposée au bureau de l’Assistante de Direction au 8ème étage de l’Immeuble Magnolia, VDN, Sud foire, lot N°30 SIPRES, Dakar contre un paiement non remboursable de cent mille (100 000) FCFA. La méthode de paiement sera par transfert WAVE, espèces ou toute autre forme de règlement acceptable. Le dossier d’appel d’offres sera adressé par courriel à l’adresse électronique indiquée sur la demande ou retiré physiquement à l’adresse ci-avant indiquée.

7.      Les Offres doivent être remises au bureau de l’Assistante de Direction au 8ème étage de l’Immeuble Magnolia, VDN Sud foire lot N°30 SIPRES Dakar au plus tard le jeudi 8 octobre 2026 à 10 heures précises, heure de Dakar. La remise des Offres par voie électronique ne sera pas permise. Toute Offre reçue après la date limite de remise des Offres sera écartée. Les Offres seront ouvertes publiquement en présence des représentants désignés des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne qui souhaitent assister à l’ouverture des Offres à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous : Salle de réunion du Projet SENRM/METE au 7ème étage de l’Immeuble Magnolia, VDN, Sud foire, lot N°30 SIPRES, Dakar le jeudi 8 octobre 2026 à 10 heures précises, heure de Dakar. Les offres devront rester valides cent-vingt (120) jours à compter de la date limite de leur dépôt.

8.       Toutes les Offres doivent être accompagnées d’une Garantie d’Offre, pour un montant de Trente millions de francs CFA (30.000.000 frs CFA). La Garantie d’Offre devra rester valide vingt-huit (28) jours après l’expiration de la validité des offres. Elle doit être délivrée par une institution bancaire ou une compagnie d’assurance agréée par le Ministère en charge des Finances ou par une institution bancaire étrangère ayant un correspondant local agréé par le Ministère en charge des Finances.

9. Une visite du site est prévue. Elle aura lieu le mercredi 23 septembre 2026 au Parc national de Niokolo koba (PNNK). Pour plus d’informations, veuillez contacter la Spécialiste en Passation des Marchés du Projet.

Les frais engagés lors de la visite du site sont à la charge des candidats.

10.   L’(les) adresse(s) auxquelles il est fait référence ci-dessus est (sont) :

Nom de l’Agence d’exécution : Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM/METE)

Nom du responsable et son titre : Mme Ndeye Coura Mbaye DIOP, Coordonnatrice du Projet

Adresse postale, le no du bureau, l’étage, le code postal, la ville, le pays: Immeuble Magnolia, 8ème étage, VDN Sud foire lot N°30 SIPRES Dakar

Numéro de téléphone et les codes de la ville et du pays : 00221 33 801 05 92/00221 78 594 82 82, CP 11500

Adresse courriel : senrm.environnement@senrm.org

Adresse du site web : senrm.senrm.org

Government of Jamaica

Ministry of Labour & Social Security

SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR INCREASED RESILIENCE AND OPPORTUNITY PROJECT (SPIRO)

Loan No.: 9652-JM

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

 

Name of Activity: Unemployment Insurance Benefit Manager.

Reference No.: JM-MLSS-564492-CS-INDV

The Government of Jamaica/Ministry of Labour & Social Security has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementing the Social Protection for Increased Resilience and Opportunity (SPIRO) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for an Unemployment Insurance (UI) Benefit Manager

Objective of the Consultancy:  The primary objective of this consultancy is to manage the transitional phase and UI business operations upon implementation, in accordance with the legislation, project objectives, and stakeholder agreements.

 Duration of the Consultancy: The consultancy will be full-time for two (2) years in the first instance to commence by November 2026.                                                     

Selection Method: Individual Consultant Selection Method as set out in the Procurement Regulations. The evaluation will be based on academic, technical expertise and experience as detailed in the Terms of Reference.

Availability of the Documents:             The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the consultancy is available for download on the following Government website: www.gojep.gov.jm

Submission Date & Time:                    CVs must be submitted online via www.gojep.gov.jm on or before September 23, 2026, at 4:00 p.m.

To participate in the opportunity, the service provider must first be registered on the Government’s Electronic Procurement System at www.gojep.gov.jm.

For assistance with registration on the GOJEP portal, please contact the Ministry of Finance and the Public Service Help Desk at (876) 932-5220 or via email at opppcustomercare@mof.gov.jm.

For additional information about GOJEP, please send email to: mofprocure@mof.gov.jm.  

Contact Information:                         

Calesha Stewart Walker

Procurement Specialist

SPIRO Project

14 National Heroes Circle, Kingston 4, Jamaica

Tel: (876) 676-5819 or 876-474-3350

E-mail: calesha-stewart.walker@mlss.gov.jm

 

 The Ministry of Labour & Social Security now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in managing the Unemployment Insurance Benefit. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

procnotices.notice_text:
Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)-Djibouti

Request for Expression of Interest

 

(Consulting Services – Individual Consultant Selection)

 

Name of project: FOOD SYSTEMS RESILIENCE PROGRAM FOR EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICA)

 

Project No.: (P178566)

 

 Grant No: IDA-E 0820

 

Assignment Title: Consultant to Develop Regional IGAD Soil Information System (SIS)

Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567401-CS-INDV

The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has received financing from International Development Agency (IDA) towards the cost of the Food systems resilience program for Eastern and Southern Africa and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Grant to payments under this contract to payments under this contract: Consultant to develop regional IGAD Soil Information System (SIS)

  1. The objective of the assignment:

To develop Data Governance Framework and Data-Sharing Protocols for a Regional SIS in IGAD.

  1. Specific Objectives
  • Assess existing soil information systems, databases, standards, and institutional arrangements within IGAD Member States.
  • Develop a data sharing framework and mechanism for Soil and Fertilizer related data from MS to the regional Soil Information System to be developed

 

  1. Minimum Consultant’s qualifications and experience requirements

The consultant should be a senior expert with extensive experience in soil information systems, geospatial data management, digital agriculture, data governance, and regional data-sharing frameworks. The expert should have demonstrated experience in assessing national information systems, developing data governance frameworks, establishing interoperability standards, and facilitating multi-country data exchange initiatives.

Required Qualifications

  • Advanced university degree (Master’s or higher) in one of the following fields: Soil Science, Agronomy, Agricultural Information Systems; Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing; Data Science, Information Systems, Computer Science; Environmental Science, Land Management, or related disciplines.
  • Additional qualifications or certifications in data governance, geospatial information systems, database management, or digital transformation will be an advantage.

Professional Experience

The consultant should have:

  • At least 7 years of professional experience in soil information management, geospatial systems, agricultural data platforms, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing, assessing, or implementing Soil Information Systems (SIS), Land Information Systems, or other environmental/agricultural information systems.
  • Proven experience conducting stakeholder assessments, institutional mapping, and data availability assessments involving government institutions, research organizations, universities, laboratories, and development partners.
  • Experience developing data governance frameworks, data-sharing policies, Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs), and institutional arrangements for multi-stakeholder or multi-country platforms.
  • Strong knowledge of soil and fertilizer data systems, including soil fertility databases, soil health indicators, laboratory datasets, nutrient mapping, fertilizer recommendations, and digital soil mapping.
  • Experience in developing data standards, metadata frameworks, classification systems, and interoperability guidelines for geospatial and scientific datasets.
  • Practical experience with GIS databases, database management systems, cloud-based data platforms, and web-based geospatial portals.
  • Experience in assessing and applying open data standards, APIs, data exchange protocols, and system interoperability approaches.
  • Experience working with regional organizations, governments, research institutions, or international development organizations on agricultural data initiatives.
  1. The Consulting Services Contract is expected to be for a period of 120 calendar days from the date of contract commencement.
  2. The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) now invites individuals to express their interest in providing the services. Interested individuals must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of Academic qualifications, and Professional Qualifications.
  3. An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (Regulations).
  4. Interested individuals may obtain further information at the address below from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday EAT).

Expression of interest shall be sent by e-mail by September/20/2026 at 1700hours EAT to:procurement@igad.int copy: hassan.salah@igad.int , with subject line ‘‘FSRP- Consultant to develop regional IGAD Soil Information System (SIS), CONTRACT NO-.: DJ-IGAD-567401-CS-INDV’’.

procnotices.notice_text:
Invitation for Bids

Information Systems

(Design, Supply and Installation)

Purchaser: Yantai Marine Economic Research Institute

Project: China Food (Shandong Yantai Aquatic Products) Safety Demonstration Project

Contract title: YT-GS-4B: Capacity Building for Digital Food Safety Supervision

Country: The People’s Republic of China

Loan No.: 9214-CN

RFP No: YT-GS-4B

Issued on: May 25, 2026

1.        The People’s Republic of China has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of China Food (Shandong Yantai Aquatic Products) Safety Demonstration Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract [1]for YT-GS-4B: Capacity Building for Digital Food Safety Supervision.

2.       The CITIC International Tendering Co., Ltd. now invites sealed Proposals from eligible Proposers for the following Information System and related services.

      Contract No. and Name: YT-GS-4B: Capacity Building for Digital Food Safety Supervision

Source of Funds: World Bank Loan

Key Contents of the Contract: Aquatic Product Quality Traceability Platform, Foodborne Disease Surveillance System, Municipal Food Safety Big Data Platform, Food Safety Supervision Platform, and Food Safety Public Service Platform.

Reference budget: CNY 19.25 million

Delivery Time: 12 months

3.       The procurement process will be conducted through national competitive procurement using Request for Proposals (RFP) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (December 2020) (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4.       Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the bidding documents. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 80 % and for Bid cost: 20 %.

5.        Interested eligible Proposers may obtain further information from CITIC International Tendering Co., Ltd. via email (Contact Email: Li Yaqian liyq@ck.citic.com, orShan Dandan, shandd@ck.citic.com). and inspect the request for proposals document during office hours 9:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. and 1:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. (Beijing Time) from May 25, 2026 to September 17, 2026(except weekends and public holidays) at the address given below.

6.       The request for proposals document in Chinese may be purchased by interested eligible Proposers upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a nonrefundable fee of CNY 1500.

7.    Qualifications requirements are as follows.

History of non-performing contracts: Non-performance of a contract did not occur as a result of Proposer’s default since 1st January 2021.

Suspension: Not under suspension based on execution of a Proposal Securing Declaration or Proposal Securing Declaration  pursuant to ITP 4.7 and ITP 20.1

Pending Litigation: Proposer’s financial position and prospective long term profitability still sound according to criteria established in 2.3.1 below and assuming that all pending litigation will be resolved against the Proposer.

Litigation History: From January 1, 2021 to the proposal submission deadline,the total amount of pending claims, arbitration, or other litigation shall not exceed 50% of the proposer's net assets.

Note: The proposer shall provide accurate information in the proposal reflecting any litigation or arbitration arising from contracts completed or being performed over the past five (5) years. A continuing history of such occurrences against the proposer or any JV member may result in rejection of the proposal.

Bank’s SEA and/or SH Disqualification: At the time of Contract Award, not subject to disqualification by the Bank for non-compliance with SEA/ SH obligations.

Historical Financial Performance: Submission of audited balance sheets or if not required by the law of the Proposer’s country, other financial statements acceptable to the Purchaser, for the last  [3 ] years (2022-2024) to demonstrate the current soundness of the Proposers financial position and its prospective long term profitability.

Average Annual Turnover: Minimum average annual turnover of CNY 48 million, calculated as total certified payments received for contracts  in progress or completed, within the last( 3 )  years(2022-2024) .

Financial  Resources: (i) The Proposer shall demonstrate that it has access to, or has available, liquid assets, unencumbered real assets, lines of credit, and other financial means (independent of any contractual advance payment) sufficient to meet the cash flow requirements for the contract estimated as CNY 9.5 million for the subject contract(s) net of the Applicants other commitments.

(ii) The audited balance sheets or, if not required by the laws of the Applicant’s country, other financial statements acceptable to the Employer, for the last 3 years shall be submitted and must demonstrate the current soundness of the Proposer's financial position and indicate its prospective long-term profitability. 

General Experience: Experience under Information System contracts in the role of prime supplier, management contractor, JV member, or subcontractor for at least the last____five____ [__5__] years prior to the applications submission deadline.

Specific Experience: A minimum number of 3 similar contracts specified below that have been satisfactorily and substantially completed (substantial completion should be based on at least 80 percent or more completed) as a prime contractor, joint venture member, management contractor or subcontractor between January 1,2023 and Application submission deadline: 

 (i) 3 contracts with total value equal or more than CNY 40 million, with at least one contract for CNY 15 million;

 (ii) Each contract should  include the following key areas:

1.Experience of implementation of IT platforms for government institutions;

2.Experience of integration of different IT applications, data sources and other digital; inputs to generate a comprehensive decision making dashboards;

3.Confirmation that no failures of previous IT platforms have occurred. 

Qualification Requirements:

(1) Holding a Capability Maturity Model Integration Level 4 (CMMI4) certification or above;

(2) Holding a CCRC Information Security Service Qualification Certification (Information System Security Integration Service) Level 2 or above;

(3) Holding ISO 9001 Quality Management System Certification, ISO 27001 Information Security Management System Certification, ISO 20000 Information Technology Service Management System Certification, and ISO 14001 Environmental Management System Certification.

8.       Proposals must be delivered to the address below on or before 9: 30 am, September 17, 2026. Electronic procurement will not be permitted. Late Proposals will be rejected. The outer Proposal envelopes marked “ORIGINAL PROPOSAL”, and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PART” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Proposers’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on 9: 30 am, September 17, 2026. All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Purchaser until the second public Proposals opening..

9.       All Proposals must be accompanied by a Proposal Security of CNY 350,000.00.

10.    Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful Proposer’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the request for proposal document.

procnotices.notice_text:
Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)-Djibouti

Request for Expression of Interest

(Consulting Services – Individual Consultant Selection)

 

Name of project: FOOD SYSTEMS RESILIENCE PROGRAM FOR EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICA

 

Project No.: (P178566)

 

 Grant No: IDA-E 0820

 

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy for The Development of an Interactive Dashboard for The IGAD Region Food Systems Resilience Analysis

Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567385-CS-INDV

The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has received financing from International Development Agency (IDA) towards the cost of the Food systems resilience program for Eastern and Southern Africa and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Grant to payments under this contract: Consultancy for The Development of an Interactive Dashboard for The IGAD Region Food Systems Resilience Analysis

1.The objective of the assignment:

The objective is to enhance evidence based decision-making on food systems resilience across the IGAD region by transforming the IGAD Food Systems Resilience Analysis Framework and its 2024 evidence base into an accessible, interactive and sustainable analytical tool.

2. Specific objectives

  1. Consolidate, harmonize and quality assure the food systems resilience data covering fourteen (14) years across the seven (7) IGAD Member States addressed in the 2024 report.
  2. Design and develop an interactive, user friendly dashboard that operationalizes the IGAD Food Systems Resilience Analysis Framework and visualizes resilience indicators, trends and cross country comparisons.
  3. Deploy the dashboard on IGAD infrastructure and ensure its interoperability with existing IGAD data systems and platforms.
  4. Build the capacity of IGAD staff to operate, update, maintain and further develop the dashboard beyond the assignment.

3. Minimum Consultant’s qualifications and experience requirements

  • The Consultant should have a Master Degree in Computer Science or ICT with demonstrated experience in building interactive dashboards and data visualizations; proficiency in modern visualization and web technologies; GIS/geospatial visualization capability an advantage.
  • The consultant should have at least 7 years demonstrated experience designing and developing interactive data dashboards or analytical web platforms, ideally in food security, climate, agriculture or resilience domains.
  • Proven experience consolidating and harmonizing multi country, multi-year datasets.
  • Prior work in Africa and, preferably, the IGAD/Horn of Africa region.
  • Demonstrated capacity building and knowledge transfer experience.
  • Have general experience relevant to the assignment (data platforms / dashboards; food security, climate or resilience analytics)
  • Specific experience developing interactive data dashboards and consolidating multi-country, multi-year datasets

 

4. The Consulting Services Contract is expected to be for a period of 150 Calendar Days from the date of contract signature.

5. The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) now invites individuals to express their interest in providing the services. Interested individuals must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of Academic qualifications, and Professional Qualifications.

6. An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (Regulations).

7. Interested individuals may obtain further information at the address below from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday EAT).

Expression of interest shall be sent by e-mail by 20th of September, 2026 at 1700hours EAT to: procurement@igad.int copy: Hassan.salah@igad.int , with subject line ‘‘FSRP/ : Consultancy for The Development of an Interactive Dashboard for The IGAD Region Food Systems Resilience Analysis Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567385-CS-INDV

REPUBLIQUE DU SENEGAL

Un Peuple – Un But – Une Foi

------------------

MINISTERE DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT ET DE LA TRANSITION ECOLOGIQUE (METE)

-------------------

PROJET DE GESTION DES RESSOURCES NATURELLES AU SENEGAL (SENRM)

 

Avis Spécifique d’Appel d’Offres (AA0)

 

Appel d’Offres pour Fournitures

(Processus à Une Enveloppe)

 

 

Appel d’Offres No : F_SENRM/ENV_074/ Réf. SYGMAP : F_SENRM_005

Projet : Projet de Gestion des Ressources naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM/METE)

Acheteur : Projet de Gestion des Ressources naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM/METE)

Pays : Sénégal

Intitulé du Marché : Acquisition de matériels et d’outillages techniques (matériels d’évaluation des ressources forestières, outils professionnels de communication en milieu forestier) en deux (2) lots

Crédit No : IDA-71890

Emis le : Septembre 2026

 

  1. L’Etat du Sénégal a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le Projet de Gestion des Ressources naturelles au Sénégal (SENRM/METE), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché n° F_SENRM/ENV_074 / Réf. SYGMAP : F_SENRM_005, relatif à l’acquisition de matériels et d’outillages techniques (matériels d’évaluation des ressources forestières, outils professionnels de communication en milieu forestier), réparti en deux (2) lots ainsi qu’il suit :
  • Lot 1 : matériels technologiques ;
  • Lot 2 : techniques de débordement.

Le soumissionnaire peut soumettre une offre pour les lots ou le lot de son choix.

2. Le projet SENRM sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir les matériels et outillages techniques (matériels d’évaluation des ressources forestières, outils professionnels de communication en milieu forestier) et, suivant le délai de livraison et au lieu indiqués dans le DAO.

Les exigences en matière de qualification sont :

a. Capacité financière :

Le Candidat doit fournir la preuve écrite qu’il satisfait aux exigences ci-après :

- Fournir les états financiers des trois dernières années (2023, 2024, 2025) dûment certifiés par un expert-comptable ou un cabinet agréé par l’ONECCA (Ordre National des Experts Comptables et Comptables Agréés) du Sénégal ou un organisme assimilé, pour chaque lot.

- Avoir réalisé un chiffre d’affaires annuel moyen au cours des trois (03) dernières années (2023, 2024 et 2025) au moins égal à :

  • Cent-quatre-vingt-trois millions sept cent cinquante mille (183 750 000) F CFA pour le lot 1, matériels technologiques ;
  • Cent treize millions trois cent quatre-vingt-cinq mille (113 385 000) F CFA pour le lot 2, outillages techniques.

                           b. Capacité technique et Expérience :

Le candidat doit prouver, document à l’appui, qu’il satisfait aux exigences de capacité technique ci-après :

Prouver, documentation à l’appui, qu’il satisfait aux exigences d’expérience ci-après : 

Deux (2) marchés similaires exécutés par le candidat au cours des cinq (05) dernières années (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 et 2025) pour un montant au moins égal à :

  • Quatre-vingt-dix-huit millions (98 000 000) F CFA pour le lot 1, matériels technologiques ;
  • Soixante millions quatre cent soixante-douze mille (60 472 000) F CFA pour le lot 2, outillages techniques.
  • 3. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence nationale (AON) telle que définie dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale de septembre 2025, et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.
  •  4. Les soumissionnaires éligibles et intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations auprès de la Spécialiste en passation des marchés du Projet SENRM/METE ; adresse électronique : passationdemarches.senrmmeddte@gmail.com et prendre connaissance des documents d’Appel d’offres durant les heures de bureau (du lundi au vendredi) de 09h 00 à 17h 00, à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous.
  • 5. Les Soumissionnaires intéressés et éligibles peuvent obtenir un dossier d’appel d’offres complet en français, en formulant une demande écrite à l’adresse mentionnée ci-après : bureau de l’Assistante de Direction au 8ème étage de l’immeuble Magnolia, Voie de dégagement Nord, Sud Foire, Lot N°30 SIPRES, Dakar et contre un paiement non remboursable de cinquante mille (50 000) francs CFA par FAITES SIGNE DE LA MAIN. Le document d’appel d’offres sera adressé par courriel à l’adresse électronique indiquée sur la demande ou retiré physiquement à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessus. Un exemplaire du DAO sera disponible sur place pour la consultation gratuite. Par respect aux principes de transparence et d’égalité de traitement des candidats, tout candidat qui, décide de déposer une offre, devra obligatoirement payer le coût du DAO.
  • 6. Les offres devront être soumises à l’adresse de retrait du DAO ci-dessus, au plus tard le Mardi 06 octobre 2026, à 10 heures précises, heure de Dakar. La soumission des offres par voie électronique ne sera pas autorisée. Les offres remises en retard ne seront pas acceptées. Les offres seront ouvertes publiquement en présence des représentants des Soumissionnaires et de toute personne choisissant d’être présente à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous, à 10 heures précises, heure de Dakar, le Mardi 06 octobre 2026. Les offres devront restées valides quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours à compter de la date limite de leur dépôt.
  • 7. Toutes les offres doivent comprendre une Garantie de l’Offre, pour un montant de :
  • Trois millions cent mille (3 100 000) F CFA pour le lot 1, matériels technologiques ;
  • Un million huit cent mille (1 800 000) F CFA pour le lot 2, outillages techniques.

procnotices.notice_text:
Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)-Djibouti

Request for Expression of Interest

 

(Consulting Services – Individual Consultant Selection)

 

Name of project: FOOD SYSTEMS RESILIENCE PROGRAM FOR EASTERN AND SOUTHERN AFRICA)

 

Project No.: (P178566)

 

 Grant No: IDA-E 0820

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy for compiling baseline information on soil/fertilizer policies, fertilizer usage and soil health best practices in IGAD Region

Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-567394-CS-INDV

The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has received financing from International Development Agency (IDA) towards the cost of the Food systems resilience program for Eastern and Southern Africa and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Grant to payments under this contract: Consultancy for compiling baseline information on soil/fertilizer policies, fertilizer usage and soil health best practices in IGAD Region

  1. Objectives of the Assignment

The main objectives of the assignment are:

  1. To Assess existing policy, institutional, financial and technical opportunities and gaps affecting fertilizer access and sustainable soil management.
  2. To map out the current status of soil health management initiatives, including: Soil fertility management, Soil conservation; Integrated Soil Fertility Management (ISFM), Climate-smart soil management, Regenerative agriculture, Organic nutrient management, Precision agriculture.
  3. Document available soil information systems including, Soil laboratories; Soil testing services
  4. To document best practices, innovations and success stories on sustainable soil and fertilizer management.
  5. Recommend directions for strengthening regional collaboration, policy harmonization and investment.
  1. Scope of the consulting services and specific tasks

The study will focus on the IGAD Region and Member states including Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Uganda.

The specific tasks will include: 

  1. Map out the existing soil and fertilizer policies, fertilizer usage and soil health best practices in IGAD Region
  2. Literature review and data collection from governments, research institutions, development partners and regional organizations
  3. Preparation of Data collection tool and Key informant interviews with relevant stakeholders;
  4. Conduct a Review of existing Regional and national policies including gap analysis and recommendations for harmonization and investment, strategies or guidelines, including cross border agreements between countries. Regional inventory of soil and fertilizer policies, fertilizer use and consumption and recommendation systems, Soil health status profile for each Member State; database of soil laboratories and information systems, regional best practices.
  5. Validation of compiled information with Member States

3. Minimum Consultant’s qualifications and experience requirements

  • The consultant should possess 5 years of experience in Agriculture, Soil Science, Agronomy, Plant Nutrition, Natural Resource Management and communication skills.
  • Clear understanding of Regional Policy processes and experience policy analyses.
  • Clear understanding of Good Agricultural Practices related to soil Health and Fertilizer use efficiency.
  • Experience in Integrated Soil Fertility Management, ISFM Practices.
  • Experience in IGAD Region Agro-ecology and Integrated Sustainable Land and Management
  • Good knowledge of African agricultural policy frameworks, including CAADP, the Africa Fertilizer and Soil Health Action Plan, and sustainable land management initiatives.
  • Good Communication, analytical and Reporting Skills.

4. The Consulting Services Contract is expected to be for a period of Six (6) calendar months from the contract commencement date.

5.The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) now invites individuals to express their interest in providing the services. Interested individuals must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of Academic qualifications, and Professional Qualifications.

6. An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated November 2020 (Regulations).

7. Interested individuals may obtain further information at the address below from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday EAT).

Expression of interest shall be sent by e-mail by 20th of September, 2026 at 1700hours EAT to:procurement@igad.int copy: hassan.salah@igad.int , with subject line ‘‘FSRP- Consultancy for compiling baseline information on soil/fertilizer policies, fertilizer usage and soil health best practices in IGAD Region, CONTRACT NO-.: DJ-IGAD-567394-CS-INDV ’’.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

  1. ASSIGNMENT PARTICULARS

Country

Republic of Uzbekistan

Client / Borrower

Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF)

Implementing Agency

Education Loan Financing Fund Management Department

(ELFFMD) within MEF

Program

EduImkon: Redesigning Opportunity, Delivering Education Equity Program

Grant Number

Grant . TF0C8875

Assignment Title

Assessment of the digital student loan platform in Uzbekistan

Selection Method

Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) — World Bank

Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers

Assignment Duration

2 to 3 months from the date of contract signing

REOI Reference

UZ-MEF-16-CS-CQS

EOI Submission Deadline

September 17, 2026, at 18:00 hours Tashkent time

  1. BACKGROUND

The Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan is implementing reforms to expand equitable access to higher education and strengthen the effectiveness and inclusiveness of student financing. In this context, the US$2 million World Bank-financed Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) supports the preparation and implementation readiness of the Student Loan Program through analytical work, institutional capacity building, implementation support, and policy development.

As the Student Loan Program increasingly relies on digital processes, a comprehensive assessment of the Digital Student Loan Platform is required to evaluate its functionality, usability, accessibility, interoperability, data governance, privacy, cybersecurity, and technical and operational performance. The assessment will identify key gaps and bottlenecks and provide practical, prioritized recommendations to improve the platform, strengthen digital integration and data management, enhance security and user experience, and support efficient, inclusive, and user-centred delivery of student financing services.

To this end, the Government intends to engage a qualified Digital/IT Consulting Firm or specialized technology company to conduct the assessment and develop an evidence base and roadmap for the further digital transformation and development of the Student Loan Program.

  1. DISBURSEMENT-LINKED RESULTS IN SCOPE

DLI

DLR

Description and Formula

Disbursement Value

DLI 1

Inception report and Work plan

Inception Report presenting the detailed methodology, assessment framework, data and information requirements, stakeholder engagement approach, quality assurance procedures, risk management measures, and detailed work plan for the assignment. The report shall confirm the proposed approach to assessing platform functionality, accessibility and user experience, interoperability and data governance, privacy and cybersecurity, technical and operational performance, and international benchmarking.

10%

DLI 2

Digital Student Loan Platform Assessment Report

A comprehensive assessment report presenting the findings of the review of the Digital Student Loan Platform. The report shall cover platform functionality and digital business processes; accessibility, usability, user experience and inclusive digital services; system integration and interoperability; data governance, data ownership, data quality, data retention and data sharing; privacy and data protection; cybersecurity and information security; technical architecture, system performance, operational resilience and business continuity; and key technical, operational and user-related challenges.

The report shall also include the results of international benchmarking against relevant GovTech good practices and comparable digital student financing platforms, where appropriate.

 

30%

DLI 3

Digital Transformation Recommendations and Reform Priorities

Based on the assessment findings, the Consulting Firm shall prepare a consolidated set of evidence-based recommendations for improving the Digital Student Loan Platform and supporting digital processes. The recommendations shall address functional, technical, operational, accessibility, user experience, interoperability, data governance, privacy, cybersecurity, institutional, and capacity-related improvements.

The deliverable shall include a prioritized implementation framework covering short-term (1–2 years), medium-term (3–5 years), and long-term (5+ years) measures, including proposed sequencing, institutional responsibilities, implementation dependencies, indicative timelines, resource and capacity requirements, and key implementation risks.

The recommendations shall incorporate relevant stakeholder feedback received through the validation process.

 

40%

DLI 4

Final Assessment Report and Policy Recommendations

Consolidated Final Report incorporating the findings and recommendations from the preceding deliverables and comments received from the Client, MEF, PIU, the World Bank, and other relevant stakeholders. The Final Assessment Report shall include an executive summary, key assessment findings, identified gaps and risks, international benchmarking results, prioritized recommendations, and conclusions regarding the future development and improvement of the Digital Student Loan Platform.

 

15%

DLI 5

Capacity Building Workshop and Presentation of Final Results

Documentation of the structured knowledge-transfer workshop for government staff, including workshop materials, participant list, and summary note.

The Consulting Firm shall prepare and deliver:

Technical Presentation (up to 30 slides) summarizing the assessment methodology, analytical findings, conclusions, recommendations, and supporting evidence for technical stakeholders.

Executive Presentation (up to 10 slides) including an Executive Summary for consultations with international experts, senior government officials, the World Bank, and other development partners.

5%

  1. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The objective is to engage a qualified consulting firm to serve as to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the Digital Student Loan Platform and the digital processes supporting the Student Loan Program in the Republic of Uzbekistan. The assessment will examine the platform's functionality, usability, accessibility, interoperability, data governance, privacy, cybersecurity, and technical and operational performance, with a focus on identifying gaps, bottlenecks, risks, and opportunities for improvement. The assignment will provide an evidence base for strengthening the platform's effectiveness, reliability, security, inclusiveness, and user-centred service delivery.

SERVICES REQUIRED

The selected firm will be required to perform the following main tasks, as detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) to be provided to the shortlisted firm:

1. Assessment of platform functionality and digital business processes with covering of the full digital student loan lifecycle, including registration, application submission, document management, verification, application processing, approval, loan administration, application tracking, notifications, reporting, workflow management, user roles, and automation of administrative processes.

 2. Assessment of accessibility, user experience and inclusive digital services of the Digital Student Loan Platform from the perspectives of students and other relevant users.

 3. Assessment of integration, interoperability, data governance, privacy and cybersecurity with relevant government, education, financial, identity, employment, tax, and other information systems, as well as its data governance, privacy, data protection, and cybersecurity arrangements.

 4. Technical and operational performance assessment and international benchmarking including the technical architecture, infrastructure, scalability, availability, reliability, performance, maintenance, technical support, operational resilience, and business continuity of the Digital Student Loan Platform.

 5. Development of digital policy recommendations and reform priorities addressing functional, technical, operational, accessibility, user experience, interoperability, data governance, privacy, cybersecurity, institutional, and capacity-related issues identified through the assessment.

 6. Final Presentation and Validation of Recommendations with the assessment findings, international benchmarking results, conclusions, and proposed digital policy recommendations and reform priorities to MEF, MHESI, PIU, the World Bank, participating financial institutions, higher education institutions, and other relevant stakeholders.

The assignment shall be completed within 2 to 3 months from contract signing. Deliverables include: (i) Inception report and Work plan; (ii)Digital Student Loan Platform Assessment Report; (iii)Digital Transformation Recommendations and Reform Priorities; (iv) Final Assessment Report and Policy Recommendations; (v)Capacity Building Workshop and Presentation of Final Results and (vi) Supporting Annexes.

  1. ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS
    1. Entity Type

This assignment is open to legally registered consulting firms, research organizations, and audit firms. Individual consultants are not eligible to apply.

    1. Registration in Uzbekistan

Firms duly registered in the Republic of Uzbekistan or with a registered local presence (branch, representative office, or subsidiary) are encouraged to confirm this in their EOI. Foreign firms without local registration may still apply but must demonstrate a credible plan for establishing local registration or a teaming arrangement with a locally registered entity prior to contract award, in accordance with the applicable legislation of Uzbekistan. MEF reserves the right to require evidence of local registration or a signed teaming agreement as a condition of contract award.

    1. World Bank Eligibility

The firm must not appear on the World Bank's list of debarred firms and individuals. Firms from all countries, except those subject to restrictions under applicable World Bank policies, may apply.

    1. Conflict of Interest

Firms that have been involved, directly or through affiliated entities, in the design, development, or implementation of any of the systems or programs whose results are to be verified under this assignment are not eligible to apply. Any actual or potential conflict of interest must be disclosed in the EOI.

  1. SHORTLISTING CRITERIA

Given the nature of this assignment, both the firm's organizational experience and the qualifications of the proposed key personnel are material to the shortlisting decision. Verification assignments under PforR instruments are highly dependent on the specific knowledge and competence of individual experts, and a strong institutional profile does not compensate for insufficiently qualified key staff. For this reason, ELFFMD will assess team composition at the shortlisting stage on a pass/fail threshold basis, alongside the firm-level criteria. The full scored evaluation of key personnel will be conducted at the proposal stage in accordance with the RFP evaluation criteria.

The shortlisting criteria are structured in two parts: Part A covers firm-level qualifications assessed on a scored basis; Part B covers key personnel assessed on a pass/fail threshold basis. Only firms satisfying all Part B thresholds will be placed on the shortlist, regardless of their Part A score.

  1. CONTENT OF THE EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Interested firms must submit their Expression of Interest in English. The EOI shall not exceed 30 pages, excluding CVs and supporting annexes, and must include the following:

  • Cover letter on firm letterhead, signed by an authorized representative, confirming the firm's interest and eligibility.
  • Firm profile: legal name, country of incorporation, registration number, year of establishment, and description of core business activities.
  • Evidence of legal registration in Uzbekistan or a registered local presence, if applicable; or a statement of intent to establish registration or a teaming arrangement with a locally registered entity prior to contract award.
  • Summary of relevant experience: a table listing at least two completed contracts of similar nature within the last seven years, with client name, assignment title, contract value, dates, and description of scope including DLR or RBF elements where applicable. Supporting documentation (completion certificates, client reference letters, or contract excerpts) is encouraged.
  • CVs of the proposed Team Leader and Information Systems Architect / Interoperability Expert, each not exceeding two pages, demonstrating compliance with the Part B thresholds in Section 7. CVs must be signed by the proposed expert.
  • Declaration signed by an authorized representative confirming: (a) no conflict of interest as defined in Section 6.4; (b) the firm is not listed on the World Bank debarment list; and (c) the firm is not registered in any jurisdiction on the list of offshore zones under Uzbek law.

CVs for the Data Governance and Cybersecurity Expert, Digital Accessibility and User Experience (UX) Expert and Digital Public Services / Business Process Analyst are not required at the EOI stage. All five key personnel CVs will be required in full at the proposal stage.

  1. SELECTION PROCESS AND BANK REVIEW ARRANGEMENTS

This assignment is procured using the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method under the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. The estimated contract value of US$80,000 falls below the applicable prior review threshold; accordingly, this assignment is subject to World Bank post review only. MEF is responsible for conducting the selection process in accordance with the Procurement Regulations, and the World Bank may review procurement records at any time during post review supervision.

The selection process will proceed as follows. ELFFMD will evaluate all EOIs received against the shortlisting criteria in Section 7. Firms that do not meet all Part B pass/fail thresholds will be excluded from further consideration. Among the remaining firms, ELFFMD will rank them against the Part A scored criteria and identify the firm with the best overall qualifications. The highest-ranked qualified firm will be invited to submit a combined technical and financial proposal and, if found satisfactory, to enter into contract negotiations. MEF reserves the right to approach the next-ranked firm if the first-ranked firm's proposal is found unsatisfactory or if negotiations are unsuccessful.

MEF reserves the right to annul this selection process at any stage without incurring any obligation to applicants.
