procnotices.notice_text:
Republic of Liberia

Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications

Western African Regional Digital Integration Project – Series of Projects 2 Liberia (WARDIP SOP2-Liberia)

 

Project ID: P500628

 

Terms of Reference

For

Recruitment of a firm to conduct Legal & Transaction Advisor for the Structuring and Capitalization of the Amilcar Cabral Cable Consortium of Liberia (AC3-Liberia)

 

Post Title:

Legal and Transaction Advisory Consultant for AC3-Liberia.

Location of Post:

Monrovia, Liberia

 

Contract Duration:

36 weeks

Reporting Line:

WARDIP Liberia/PIU through the PIU Coordinator

 

Recruitment Type:

Local

 

Type of Contract

    Individual Consultant

X Consulting Firm (QCBS, CQS, LCS)

    Non-Consulting Service (Competitive Bidding)

 

 

1. PROJECT BACKGROUND

 

The Government of Liberia (GoL) has received financing from the World Bank for the preparation of the West Africa Regional Digital Integration Project - Series of Projects 2 Liberia (WARDIP SOP2-Liberia). This project, which will be implemented at the national level, seeks to facilitate increased broadband access and usage in preparation for regional digital markets integration in West Africa.

 

WARDIP SOP2-Liberia is the second phase of the Western Africa Regional Development Integration Program series of projects (DTfA – WARDIP), which builds consensus and momentum around the vision for achieving a Single Digital Market (SDM) in Africa. It is envisioned that the project will lead to an increased secure flow of digital services within and between participating countries in Western Africa. By the end of the SOP, foundations of a SDM in Western Africa in line with the AU SDM are expected to be in place.

 

WARDIP SOP2 builds on, and will run parallel to, investments in DTfA/WARDIP SOP1, further extending cross-border and backbone connectivity, data markets and online market environment in additional countries. It aims to increase broadband access and usage in participating countries and to advance the integration of digital markets in Western Africa and is structured to have 5 components.

 

  • Component I. Connectivity Market Development and Integration: This component aims to provide infrastructure financing and support for an enhanced enabling environment to develop the regional broadband connectivity market.
  • Component II: Data Market Development and Integration: This component aims to build trust in online transactions and strengthen the security and resilience of digital infrastructure and systems, focused on focuses on enabling secure, cross-border data exchange, storage, and processing to support regional access to data-driven services, innovation, and infrastructure. 
  • Component III. Online Market Development and Integration: This component aims to support the development of a robust regional online market, with a focus on boosting service uptake for an integrated SDM.
  • Component IV. Project Management and Implementation Support. This component would provide technical assistance and capacity support for program preparation and implementation.
  • Component V. Contingent Emergency Response. The component is included to help participating countries respond swiftly to eligible crises and emergencies, in case of urgent need of assistance or capacity constraints.

 

Access to affordable, reliable, and resilient international internet connectivity is essential for Liberia’s digital transformation, economic growth, and social inclusion. Over the past decade, Liberia has significantly strengthened its digital infrastructure through its connection to the Africa Coast to Europe (ACE) submarine cable system, financed under the World Bank–supported West Africa Regional Communications Infrastructure Program (WARCIP). The ACE system has substantially expanded international bandwidth capacity, reduced wholesale prices, and enabled growth across Liberia’s digital economy.

 

Despite these improvements, Liberia currently relies almost entirely on a single submarine cable. As demand for data and digital services continues to rise—driven by increased mobile data usage, digital government rollout, enterprise connectivity needs, and cloud adoption—dependence on one international link exposes the country to serious risks, including outages, rising operational costs, and vulnerability to disruptions. Strengthening the redundancy, diversity, and resilience of Liberia’s international connectivity has therefore become a national priority.

 

To address this strategic need, the Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MoPT) and with support under the West Africa Regional Digital Integration Program (WARDIP), is advancing plans for a second international submarine cable landing in Liberia. While the specific system has not yet been finalized, the new submarine cable initiative is expected to provide the country with additional capacity, enhanced redundancy, improved competition, and greater resilience—supporting Liberia’s long-term digital transformation ambitions.

 

Planning for the second cable has been informed by a multi-country technical and financial feasibility assessment conducted by TACTIS, which examined future international capacity needs, technology options, landing site considerations, commercial structures, and governance arrangements across participating West African countries. For Liberia, the assessment confirmed that a second submarine cable is both technically viable and commercially justified. It identified strong and growing bandwidth demand and the need to reduce the risks associated with dependence on ACE. These findings reinforce the urgency of establishing a second connection and the importance of designing a sound ownership, governance, and financing structure.

 

To ensure efficient, transparent, and sustainable management of Liberia’s stake in the future cable system, the Government and private sector actors have agreed to establish a dedicated Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)—the Amilcar Cabral Cable Consortium of Liberia (AC3-Liberia). Liberia’s major Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) and Internet Service Providers (ISPs) have signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) expressing their intention to jointly establish and capitalize the SPV. The Government of Liberia will participate as a minority shareholder, providing policy alignment and strategic oversight while e

nsuring that ownership and operational control remain led by the private sector—consistent with global best practices for submarine cable wholesale governance.

 

The SPV will ultimately hold Liberia’s ownership interest in the second submarine cable system, including the landing station and any associated terrestrial infrastructure. To become operational, AC3-Liberia requires a complete set of legal, regulatory, commercial, and financial structuring actions, including incorporation, preparation of foundational corporate instruments, design of governance arrangements, valuation of contributions (including in-kind assets), financial modeling, assessing the need for additional investors, and preparing the SPV for financial close. The SPV must be designed to remain fully viable even if no external investors join initially, while retaining flexibility to accommodate new private-sector or development finance institution (DFI) participation in the future.

 

To support this effort, the Government of Liberia seeks to engage a single qualified advisory firm to provide integrated legal and transaction advisory services. The Advisor will assist the Government and the prospective shareholders in establishing AC3-Liberia as a legally compliant, financially sound, and commercially sustainable SPV capable of achieving financial close for the second submarine cable. The integrated nature of the assignment ensures that legal, commercial, and financial dimensions are fully aligned, reducing risks and enabling the creation of a robust and professionally governed entity that will safeguard Liberia’s long-term international connectivity.

   

2. OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT

 

The objective of this assignment is to structure AC3-Liberia as a financially viable, commercially sustainable, and operationally sound Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) that reflects a majority private-sector ownership model with the Government of Liberia participating as a minority shareholder. The Advisor will provide integrated legal, commercial, and financial structuring support to ensure that the SPV is established on a sound foundation and is capable of achieving financial close and operational readiness for the new cable landing.

 

A core objective is the legal establishment and operationalization of AC3-Liberia. The Advisor will lead the drafting of all corporate legal instruments—including the Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, Shareholders’ Agreement, Subscription Agreements, Governance Framework, and related documentation—and will manage the full registration process with the Liberia Business Registry and other national authorities. The assignment includes ensuring compliance with Liberian company law, telecommunications regulations, tax requirements, and all World Bank/WARDIP obligations, including safeguards, transparency, and good governance standards.

 

In parallel, the assignment aims to design and structure AC3-Liberia as a financially sustainable and bankable entity. The Advisor will assess capital requirements, develop a comprehensive financial model, and design a capital structure that reflects a majority private-sector ownership model with the Government participating as a minority shareholder. This includes valuing all shareholder contributions, incorporating the Government’s confirmed cash equity contribution, and identifying and valuing potential in-kind contributions that could strengthen the SPV’s capital base. The SPV must remain fully viable even if no additional investors join initially, while retaining flexibility to accommodate new private-sector investors or Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) should such participation later be deemed beneficial.

 

A third objective is to support investor readiness and capital mobilization options. The Advisor will assess whether attracting additional private investors or DFIs could bring financial, operational, or strategic value to the SPV. If justified, the Advisor will conduct targeted market sounding and provide recommendations on next steps. Any competitive investor selection process will only be undertaken if clearly warranted and approved by the Consortium.

 

A fourth objective is to ensure strong alignment between financial structuring and legal documentation. The Advisor will integrate legal and transaction advisory functions so that corporate instruments, commercial agreements, capitalization arrangements, IRU structures, risk allocation provisions, and governance mechanisms are coherent and mutually reinforcing. The assignment includes guiding the Government and private operators through negotiations, ensuring that all agreements are commercially sound, enforceable, and aligned with the long-term sustainability of the SPV.

 

Finally, the Advisor will guide AC3-Liberia through the process of achieving financial close and becoming fully operational. This includes preparing conditions precedent, capitalization steps, subscription arrangements, and the full set of documentation required by investors and financiers. The Advisor will prepare a complete financial close package and provide a clear roadmap for implementation, ensuring that AC3-Liberia is positioned to execute the submarine cable project effectively.

 

 

3. SCOPE OF WORK

 

The Consultant will provide comprehensive legal, commercial, and financial advisory services necessary for the establishment, structuring, operationalization, and capitalization of the Amilcar Cabral Cable Consortium of Liberia (AC3-Liberia). The scope covers all tasks required to (i) incorporate the SPV as a legally compliant entity, (ii) design and negotiate its governance and capital structure, (iii) prepare it for financial close, and (iv) ensure long-term sustainability and readiness to manage Liberia’s second international submarine cable landing.

 

This engagement includes, but is not limited to the following:

 

Phase 1: Corporate & Regulatory Foundations

 

  1. Review of Legal & Regulatory Framework: Review Liberian laws, regulations, and administrative requirements relevant to establishing and operationalizing AC3-Liberia, including company law, investment law, SPV formation requirements, telecommunications licensing, international cable-landing and access regulations, foreign/domestic ownership rules, tax obligations, and any PPP or procurement frameworks. Identify regulatory obligations applicable during establishment, operation, capitalization, and future expansion.
  2. Review of Existing MoU and Documentation: Analyze the existing non-binding MoU among the MNO/ISP members and identify any issues requiring refinement during incorporation. Review all available project documentation and identify areas requiring legal, commercial, or financial alignment before SPV formation.
  3. Initial Structuring Readiness Assessment: Review the prior technical, commercial, and financial work completed to date—including the TACTIS feasibility analysis—to validate assumptions, identify information gaps, and determine implications for SPV structuring. Provide immediate recommendations to support legal and institutional readiness.
  4. Preliminary Risk Identification: Identify major early-stage legal, commercial, financial, and governance risks and provide initial mitigation strategies, to be refined throughout subsequent phases.

 

Phase 2: Financial Feasibility, Commercial Model Options, and SPV Capital Structure

 

  1. Financial Feasibility and Model Development: Develop a comprehensive financial model aligned with the technical and commercial assumptions, emerging from the TACTIS feasibility work. The model shall include CAPEX, OPEX, lifecycle maintenance, depreciation, replacement cycles, projected revenues, cash flow performance, sensitivity tests, capital-call implications, and long-term sustainability. Coordinate with the technical team to ensure all input is consistent.
  2. Commercial Structure Assessment & Refinement: Analyze and refine practical wholesale commercial structure options appropriate for a shared landing-party SPV. These options may include variations in pricing methodologies, cost-recovery mechanisms, revenue allocation rules, and capacity assignment principles. For each model, evaluate implications for:
  • affordability and competitiveness of international capacity;
  • long-term financial sustainability of the SPV;
  • incentives for private-sector investment;
  • governance arrangements and operational complexity;
  • compatibility with potential DFI financing.

Support AC3 members in reviewing these options and facilitate consensus toward the preferred commercial structure. Once a model is agreed, translate it into the necessary financial assumptions and structuring parameters for the SPV.

  1. Capital Structure & Shareholding Design: Define capital requirements and develop a proposed capitalization structure for AC3-Liberia, including:
  • valuation of all shareholder contributions, including Government cash equity and potential in-kind contributions (e.g., rights-of-way, landing facilities, ducts, strategic assets);
  • design of shareholding arrangements consistent with majority private-sector ownership and minority Government participation;
  • capital-call mechanisms, tranche schedules, and pre-operational financing arrangements;
  • assessment of optional participation by external private investors or DFIs and implications for dilution or governance.
  1. Assessment of External Investor Participation (Optional): Where beneficial, undertake a targeted assessment of whether additional investors or DFIs should be invited to participate. Provide a recommendation to AC3 members on whether external participation adds commercial, operational, or financial value. If approved, proceed with the optional competitive process under Phase 3C.

 

Phase 3 – SPV Incorporation, Corporate Structuring, and Legal-Commercial Alignment

 

  1. Preparation of Corporate Legal Instruments: Prepare all legal instruments required for the establishment and operation of AC3-Liberia, ensuring including alignment with the selected commercial and capital structure. Documents include: the Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, Shareholders’ Agreement, Subscription Agreements, Subscription Agreement, Corporate Governance Framework, Board Charter, and any additional founding instruments or annexes needed to ensure a coherent and legally sound SPV structure.
  2. Governance and Commercial Framework Design: Translate the preferred commercial structure into governance rules, shareholder rights and obligations, decision-making arrangements, participation conditions for operators, reporting requirements, dispute-resolution mechanisms, capital-call processes, and compliance obligations. Ensure consistency with Liberian law and international practice for shared international cable landing arrangements.
  3. Alignment of Legal, Financial, and Commercial Structuring: Ensure full coherence between legal instruments, commercial terms, governance frameworks, financial model parameters, and capitalization designs. Conduct iterative joint reviews with AC3-Liberia members to harmonize assumptions and obligations across all documents.
  4. Project Implementation Manual (PIM) for the SPV: Prepare a draft PIM that serves as the operational handbook for AC3-Liberia, covering how the SPV will be governed, capitalized, and managed, and how it will carry out its responsibilities under the project. The PIM shall include the SPV's governance and decision-making structure, capitalization arrangements and equity contribution process, operational procedures, criteria and process for admitting private Licensed Telecommunications Operators as shareholders, and the legal and regulatory framework within which the SPV operates.
  5. Optional Competitive Process for External Investors: If external participation is recommended and approved:
  • develop financial and commercial sections for Initial Selection (IS) and RFP documents;
  • support evaluation criteria and financial-compliance scoring;
  • review and advise on bidder submissions.

No process will be launched unless explicitly requested by AC3-Liberia.

 

Phase 4 –Negotiation, Document Finalization, and Financial Close Preparation

 

  1. Negotiation Support: Support AC3-Liberia in negotiations with shareholders – and if applicable, external investors and DFIs. Review financing offers, term sheets, and investment commitments. Ensure all negotiated terms remain aligned with the SPV’s financial model, capital structure, and governance structure.
  2. Finalization of Corporate, Commercial, and Legal Documentation: Revise legal and commercial documents to reflect negotiation outcomes and ensure consistency with the final commercial and capitalization structure. Confirm enforceability and completeness.
  3. Financial Close Package and Roadmap: Prepare the Financial Close Package, including the financing plan, capital structure narrative, valuation summaries (cash and in-kind contributions), commercial structure and risk allocation summary, supporting model outputs, required by financiers. Develop a roadmap and checklist for financial close and support AC3-Liberia in fulfilling conditions precedent, executing equity subscription steps, and completing capitalization processes.
  4. Optional Interface Support with WARDIP Implementation: If requested, provide inputs on how AC3-Liberia’s governance, reporting, and capitalization arrangements interface with WARDIP project implementation processes (e.g., sequencing of approvals, Government equity contributions, PIU coordination).

 

Phase 5 – Final Report and Handover

 

Prepare and submit a consolidated final report, including:

  • Final legal documentation.
  • Financial model (editable with user guide)
  • Valuation assessments (cash and in-kind)
  • Commercial term sheets
  • Capital structure and financial close documents
  • Investor participation analysis (if applicable)
  • Operationalization roadmap for AC3-Liberia
  • Project Implementation Manual (PIM) for the SPV

 

4. DURATION, DELIVERABLES OF THE ASSIGNMENT, AND PAYMENT SCHEDULE 

 

The assignment is expected to last 12 months (365 days) or until financial close of AC3-Liberia, whichever occurs first.

Payments will be made upon acceptance of the following deliverables:

 

Timeline

Deliverables

Payment (%)

Commencement + 2 weeks

Inception Report and Immediate Readiness Actions

  • Inception report with methodology, work plan, and stakeholder engagement plan.
  • Rapid legal and institutional readiness assessment.
  • Review of existing technical/financial inputs (incl. TACTIS) and identification of gaps.
  • Preliminary mapping of SPV incorporation steps and responsibilities.
  • Initial risk register with mitigation measures.

10%

Commencement + 8 weeks

Financial Feasibility, Commercial Structure Options, and Draft Capital Structure

  • Draft multi-scenario financial model (CAPEX/OPEX/lifecycle/sensitivities)
  • Analysis and refinement of practical wholesale commercial structure options.
  • Draft capital structure and preliminary valuation of shareholder contributions (cash + potential in-kind).
  • Advisory note on potential role of external/DFI investors.
  • Interim structuring memo summarizing recommended direction.

20%

  • Finalization of preferred commercial structure after AC3 consultations.
  • Updated financial model reflecting agreed commercial assumptions.
  • Final recommended capital structure and draft shareholding distribution options.
  • Updated valuation note (cash and potential in-kind contributions).

  • Draft Articles of Incorporation.

  • Full Financial Close Package (financing plan, capitalization narrative, valuations, risk allocation, model outputs).
  • Checklist and roadmap for conditions precedent.

  • Operationalization advisory note.

10%

  • Closing debrief / capacity support session.

5%

 

 

 

5. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

 

The selected firm must demonstrate the capacity to deliver both legal advisory and financial/transaction advisory services under a single contract, with proven experience in structuring and operationalizing infrastructure SPVs. Specifically, the firm must meet the following criteria:

  • Registered law firm, financial advisory firm, or consortium (acting as a single contracting entity) with demonstrated ability to provide integrated legal, financial, and commercial advisory services.
  • Minimum of 10 years’ experience in infrastructure PPPs, corporate structuring, and project finance in emerging or developing markets.
  • Demonstrated expertise in telecommunications, ICT, digital infrastructure, or submarine cable/landing-station projects, including experience with shared infrastructure or wholesale access arrangements.
  • Experience advising Governments, DFIs, private operators, or regulators on the structuring of PPPs, SPVs, or infrastructure investment vehicles.
  • Proven track record in drafting and negotiating corporate legal documentation (e.g., Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, Shareholders’ Agreements, Subscription Agreements, governance frameworks).
  • Proven capability in financial structuring, including capital structure design, valuation of cash and in-kind contributions, and preparation of transactions for DFI participation.
  • Demonstrated ability to build, maintain, and stress-test financial models for large-scale infrastructure SPVs, including multi-scenario and long-term sustainability analyses.
  • Strong understanding of Liberian commercial, company, and tax law, or ability to mobilize qualified Liberian legal expertise as part of the team.

Experience working in West Africa or similar environments is an advantage.

Ability to deploy a multidisciplinary team fluent in English, available throughout the assignment.

 

5.1 KEY EXPERTS

 

The consulting firm shall provide the following key experts for the assignment:

  1. Legal & Transaction Expert as Team Leader: At least 15 years of experience in structuring PPPs, SPVs, and closing project-financed infrastructure transactions, with a strong track record in telecommunications, fiber-optic, or other digital infrastructure projects. Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams, negotiate with private operators and DFIs, and oversee both legal and commercial workstreams. Experience in Africa or similar contexts is an advantage.
  2. Senior Legal Specialist (Corporate & Regulatory): At least 10 years of experience in corporate and commercial law, including drafting Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, Shareholders’ Agreements, Subscription Agreements, and corporate governance frameworks. Experience with telecommunications regulation or digital infrastructure licensing is preferred. Expertise in Liberian law may be provided through qualified national legal counsel within the team structure.
  3. Project Finance Specialist: At least 10 years of experience in infrastructure project finance, capital structure design, valuation of cash and in-kind contributions, and preparation of transactions for DFI participation. Demonstrated experience advising on financing term sheets, investor negotiations, and financial close processes. Experience in telecommunications or digital infrastructure is preferred.
  4. Financial Modeling Specialist: At least 5 years of experience in business and financial modeling for infrastructure SPVs or PPP projects. Proven ability to build multi-scenario models incorporating CAPEX, OPEX, demand projections, cost-recovery frameworks, capital-call structures, and long-term sustainability analysis. Experience with digital infrastructure or telecommunications is an advantage.
  5. Corporate & Governance Expert – At least 7 years in designing and operationalizing governance structures for SPVs, joint ventures, or infrastructure consortia. Experience drafting governance frameworks, board charters, reporting protocols, and decision-making rules, and advising on operational readiness and shareholder interfaces.

 

The firm may propose additional non-key experts (e.g., Tax Advisor, Telecom Market Specialist, etc.) as needed to deliver the assignment. These will not be scored individually but will be considered in assessing the overall adequacy of the proposed team.

 

 

 

 

 

6. CONFIDENTIALITY

 

By accepting to take part in the invitation, the Consultant agrees to keep in confidence all information shared by the Liberian government authorities and the World Bank, whether written or oral, concerning the invitation and/or in relation to the government organizations’ business involved in this assignment which is not of public domain. The Consultant also agrees to use it only for the purposes of this activity and for no other reasons and not to disclose any of the said information to any third party.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

COUNTRY: CABO VERDE

PROJECT: Health Security Program in Western and Central Africa Project

PROJECT ID Nº: P179078

Notice Number: EOI – 035/HSP/UGPE/2025-2

 

Date: July 30, 2026

Extension Date: September 04, 2026

 

Assignment Title: Recruitment of an international consultant to carry out training in areas of national and international border health inspection.

 

1. The Government of Cabo Verde has received a financing in the amount of US$ 29.00 million from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Health Security Program in Western and Central Africa Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for: Recruitment of an international consultant to carry out training in areas of national and international border health inspection.

 

2.To strengthen the technical and operational skills of 45 animal health inspectors and field technicians  (22 women and 23 men) from the MAA’s regional offices, in modern and innovative animal health inspection techniques at national and international points of entry, enabling them to effectively apply inspection and animal health control procedures for animal products and live animals, in accordance with international standards and national legislation, thereby contributing to animal health security, public health protection, and trade facilitation.

 

3.More detailed information is provided in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment that can be obtained at the address given below, from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m. (local time), during working day, or in written at the email address below, or can be found at the following website: https://ugpe.gov.cv/concursos?projeto=P179078;/https://www.mf.gov.cv/web/mf/outras-publicacoes.

 

4.The implementing agency Integrated Project Coordination Center CCIP, now invites eligible individual consultants (Consultant) to express their interest in providing this service. Interested individuals consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services. A Letter of Interest duly signed and updated Curriculum Vitae indicating namely, description of similar assignments, experience and contact references in similar service are required.

 

  1. To be selected, the individual Consultant must have the following qualifications:
    1. Higher education, minimum bachelor’s degree, in the field of veterinary medicine
    2. Master’s degree or specialization in public health, sanitary inspection, epidemiology, or a related field will be considered an asset”.;
    3. Proven experience in the development and implementation of training programs in border inspection management, disease surveillance, and risk assessment;
    4. Proven and in-depth knowledge of the WHO Code for Terrestrial and Aquatic Animals, the Codex Alimentarius, Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures—the WTO SPS Agreement, and the International Health Regulations (IHR);

 

    1. Excellent communication, training, and facilitation skills;

 

    1. At least 10 years of relevant experience in the aforementioned field;
    2. At least 10 years of experience in the field of health inspection at border posts;
    3. At least 10 years of experience as a trainer/instructor, with a good understanding of

training methodology;

    1. Fluency in spoken and written Portuguese.

 

6.An individual consultant will be selected under the Individual Consultant Selection (ICS) method set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, July 2016 edition, revised on September 2025.

 

7. Interested Consultants may obtain further information at the emails address below from 8:00 a.m. until 16:00 p.m. (local time), during working days.

SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE (SPN)

 

Request for Proposal

 

Spectrum Management and Monitoring Equipment (Fixed and Mobile Units) for the support of National Communications Authority of Somalia (NCA), FGS.

 

(Single Stage Two Envelopes with Rated Criteria)

 

Purchaser: Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS

End User: The support of National Communications Authority of Somalia (NCA), FGS

Project: Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP)

Project ID: P176181

Contract title: Spectrum Management and Monitoring Equipment (Fixed and Mobile Units) for the support of National Communications Authority of Somalia (NCA), FGS.

Country: The Federal Republic of Somalia

RFP No: SO-MOCT-FGS-558190-NC-RFP

Submission deadline date: October 20, 2026, at 1:00 pm (Mogadishu, Somalia Time)

 

1. The Federal Government of Somalia has received for a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) to finance the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project with Project ID: P176181, and the Federal Government of Somalia intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for the Spectrum Management and Monitoring Equipment (Fixed and Mobile Units)  for the support of National Communications Authority of Somalia (NCA), FGS. No party other than the Federal Government of Somalia shall derive any rights from the financing agreement or have any claims to the proceeds of the finance. For this contract, the Federal Government of Somalia shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing.

2. Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS now invites sealed Proposals from eligible Proposers for the assignment of Spectrum Management and Monitoring Equipment (Fixed and Mobile Units) for the support of National Communications Authority of Somalia (NCA),FGS.

3. The procurement process will be conducted through international competitive procurement using Request for Proposals (RFP) with Rated Criteria as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated July 1st, 2016, revised November 2017 August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations that meet the following minimum qualification criteria;

      a) Proposer’s Financial Capability

i. The Proposer shall furnish documentary evidence that it meets the following financial requirement: the average Annual Turnover in the last three (3) years (2023, 2024 and 2025) to be not less than USD 3,000,000 (Three Million United States Dollars);

ii. Financial Resources: The Bidder must demonstrate access to, or availability of, financial resources to meet the following cash-flow requirement: Access to USD 1,000,000 within the last three (3) years (2023, 2024, 2025).

      b) Proposer’s Experience and Technical Capacity

i. The Proposer shall have a minimum of five (5) years of experience in the design, supply, installation, commissioning, and support of spectrum management and monitoring systems (fixed and mobile units), radio monitoring networks, or related regulatory technical platforms. The Proposer shall provide proven evidence of satisfactory completion of at least two (2) similar projects within the past seven (7) years involving the delivery of spectrum monitoring systems for national regulatory authorities or telecommunications operators; the Proposer shall submit at least one (1) client reference for each such successfully completed project, and each reference shall include: (a) name of the client, including address and email; (b) country of implementation; (c) year of completion; (d) description and scope of the assignment; and (e) contract value. Each reference shall be supported by documentary evidence of satisfactory completion, such as Completion Certificates, Reference Letters, or Final Acceptance Certificates.

ii. The Proposer shall demonstrate proven experience in delivering vendor-neutral spectrum monitoring and management platforms with real-time monitoring, measurement, direction-finding, and geolocation capabilities covering both fixed and mobile monitoring stations. The Proposer shall further demonstrate proven capability of operating in multi-vendor, multi-technology environments (e.g., 2G/3G/4G/5G networks and broadcast services), as well as prior work with or for telecommunications regulatory authorities on comparable assignments, including compliance with applicable ITU-R recommendations.

iii. The Proposer shall have successfully completed at least two (2) comparable contracts for the implementation of spectrum management and monitoring systems, in the public or private sector, including the supply and installation of the relevant hardware (fixed and/or mobile monitoring units), with a minimum contract value of USD 1,000,000 (One Million United States Dollars), completed within the last Five (5) years.

iv. The Proposer shall demonstrate proven international experience in the implementation of comparable systems in developing countries. Experience in delivering similar assignments in Fragile, Conflict, and Violence (FCV)-affected countries;

      c) Proposer’s Legal Requirements

i. The Proposer shall be legally registered entity in its country of origin.

4. Interested eligible Proposers may obtain further information from the PIU Procurement Unit in the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project at the Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS, procurement.ea-rdip@moct.gov.so and inspect the Request for Proposals document during office hours 10.00am to 4.00pm (Mogadishu, Somalia Local Time) at the address given below.

A pre-proposal online conference meeting will be held on;

Date:                September 14, 2026, 2026

Place :              Virtual

Link for the meeting (Zoom): https://us06web.zoom.us/j/85755689691?pwd=s2aadxDg84a8LcOgBzmJpxer7u7BTC.1    

5. A complete set of Proposal documents in English language will be provided upon request.  The document including any subsequent amendment or addition will be sent to the Proposer by e-mail. Prior registration is required for submitting clarification questions on the Proposal documents and receiving automatic notice of answers and addenda to the Proposal documents.

6. Proposals must be delivered to the address below on or before October 20, 2026, at 1:00 pm (Mogadishu, Somalia Time). Electronic proposal submissions will NOT be permitted. Late Proposals will be rejected. The outer Proposal envelopes marked “ORIGINAL PROPOSAL”, and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PART” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Proposers’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on October 20, 2026 at 1.00pm (Mogadishu, Somalia Time). All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Purchaser until the second public Proposals opening.

REPOBLIKAN’I MADAGASIKARA

Fitiavana – Tanindrazana - Fandrosoana

PRIMATURE

Office National de Nutrition

Unité du Programme National de Nutrition Communautaire

______________________________________________________

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊT

N°05/26

POUR LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN ASSISTANT EN PASSATION DE MARCHES DU FINANCEMENT ADDITIONNEL DU PROJET PARN II

 

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) en vue de financer le coût du financement additionnel de la deuxième phase du Projet d’Amélioration des Résultats Nutritionnels (PARN2) et se propose d’utiliser une partie du financement pour effectuer des paiements autorisés au titre du contrat d’un consultant individuel assistant en Passation de Marchés qui est en charge de la mise en œuvre du projet.

2. D’une manière générale, la mission du consultant est d’assister dans les fonctions de passation de marchés et de suivi des contrats/marchés.

 

         Spécifiquement, il s’agit de :

  •   Etablir les avis généraux de passation des marchés et avis de présélection, de manifestation d’intérêt et d’appel d’offres ;
  • Appuyer à l’établissement des dossiers d’appel d’offres, des demandes de propositions et des contrats de prestation (consultants, travaux et fournitures) ;
  • Lancer l’Avis d’Appel d’Offres (AAO) et mettre à disposition des soumissionnaires les DAO ;
  • Recevoir, enregistrer et envoyer des courriers et documents au niveau de la passation de marchés (offres, contrats, ordre de service, bon de commande, dossiers d’appel d’offres, lettres, ...) ;
  • Préparer et participer aux séances d’ouverture des plis et appuyer les commissions sur l’établissement des rapports d’évaluation ;
  • Rédiger les Procès-verbaux d’ouverture des plis, de négociations ;
  •  Rédiger le draft du marché/bon de commande ;
  • Préparer l’Ordre de service portant notification du marché signé et démarrage des prestations/travaux ;
  • Préparer les dossiers de marchés et contrats nécessaires à l’audit périodique de la passation des marchés ;
  •  Assurer la gestion informatisée de la passation de marchés et tenue à jour du registre des avis (AMI, AON, AOI...)

 

3. Les termes de référence détaillées du poste peuvent être envoyés aux Consultants intéressés qui en font la demande à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous. Le nom et l’adresse du Consultant devront être clairement spécifiées dans la requête

 

4. L’Unité du Programme National de Nutrition Communautaire invite maintenant les Consultants individuels admissibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications et l’expérience appropriées pour cette fonction. Le dossier de candidature devra inclure une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt, un curriculum vitae détaillé présentant notamment les références du Consultant dans l’exécution de contrats similaires, ainsi que les copies des diplômes, le(s) numéro(s) de téléphone et l’adresse électronique.

 

5. Le consultant devra répondre au profil ci-après :

 

Qualification académique :

  • Être titulaire d’un diplôme de Bacc+4 en en administration, sciences économiques, gestion ou autres domaines jugés acceptables

Expériences :

Le consultant devra justifier d’une expérience pertinente dans les domaines clés du développement de la petite enfance, répondant à l’un des critères suivants :

  • Avoir une expérience confirmée d’au moins 2 ans en passation de marchés ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance des procédures de passation de marchés des bailleurs de fonds
  • Expérience dans les projets financés par la Banque mondiale

 

Autres compétences et qualités requises :

  • Connaissance et pratique du STEP
  • Avoir une bonne maîtrise de l’outil informatique ;
  • Avoir un esprit d’analyse et de synthèse et grande capacité de rédaction ;
  • Avoir réalisé un stage dans les projets financés par la Banque mondiale
  • Être méthodique, organisé(e) et ayant une personnalité affirmée (respect de la confidentialité) ;
  • Savoir parler malagasy et français avec capacité de rédaction
  • Connaissance des logiciels Microsoft (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
  • Connaissance du français à l'oral et à l'écrit
  • La connaissance de l'anglais serait un atout
  • Expérience de travail dans les programmes de développement de la petite enfance à assise communautaire

 

6. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’investissement FPI » de Juillet 2016, Septième Edition du Septembre 2025 (« Règlement »), énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.

procnotices.notice_text:
APPEL A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊT

(SERVICES DE CONSULTANT)

SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS INDIVIDUELS

N° 10/2026/ProAGRI

 

Pays : République du TCHAD               

Numéro du Don : E3170

ID du Projet : P179238                            

Projet : Projet d’Agrobusiness et de Transformation Rurale Inclusive (ProAGRI).

 

Intitulé de la Mission : Recrutement d'un consultant individuel pour l’élaboration (i) du Manuel opérationnel de sélection et de subventionnement des Microprojets du ProAGRI — volet individus/coopératives et (ii) du Manuel opérationnel des Plateformes d'Innovation pour la mise en place et le financement des plans d'action de 13 PI (5 PI-maïs, 4 PI-arachide/sésame, 4 PI-poisson).

 

Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet d’Agrobusiness et de Transformation Rurale Inclusive (ProAGRI) et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché de recrutement d'un consultant individuel pour l’élaboration (i) du Manuel opérationnel de sélection et de subventionnement des Microprojets du ProAGRI — volet individus/coopératives et (ii) du Manuel opérationnel des Plateformes d'Innovation pour la mise en place et le financement des plans d'action de 13 PI (5 PI-maïs, 4 PI-arachide/sésame, 4 PI-poisson).

 

La Sous-composante 3.2, intitulée « Accroître l'accès au financement et à la valeur ajoutée », constitue le principal levier d'investissement productif du Projet. Elle mobilise quatre instruments complémentaires : (i) le warrantage ; (ii) les subventions de contrepartie (matching grants) organisées en quatre guichets distincts, chacun doté de son propre manuel ; (iii) le mécanisme de garantie de crédit géré par l'IFC ; (iv) les services de développement des affaires (BDS). Les Plateformes d'Innovation constituent l'instrument transversal qui met en système l'ensemble de ces guichets.

 

Le guichet PPP agro-industriels cible les partenariats entre le ProAGRI et des entreprises agro-industrielles (AIE) de grande taille qui souhaitent développer ou consolider leur ancrage dans les filières prioritaires du Tchad (maïs, sésame, arachide, poisson, volaille, dattes, etc.). Avec un plafond pouvant atteindre 5 000 000 USD par PPP (dont une subvention ProAGRI plafonnée à 2 000 000 USD) et au moins 4 PPP prévus, ce guichet vise à mobiliser l'investissement privé agro-industriel structurant pour densifier les chaînes de valeur.

Le manuel opérationnel de ce volet doit définir les critères de qualification des AIE partenaires, le processus de présélection et de négociation des conventions de PPP, les engagements réciproques (l'AIE apporte le cofinancement privé et s'engage sur des objectifs de sourcing auprès des producteurs locaux), les modalités de décaissement par tranches conditionnées par les résultats, et le dispositif de suivi et d'audit.

 

Les Plateformes d'Innovation (PI) ne sont pas des guichets de financement mais des espaces de travail multi-acteurs — producteurs, transformateurs, commerçants, IFP, services techniques, CCIAMA — où sont identifiés les verrous des filières, expérimentées des solutions techniques, contractualisées des alliances commerciales et diffusées les innovations validées. Chaque PI est ancrée dans une filière et un territoire, suit un cycle annuel de 12 mois en sept étapes, et dispose d'une enveloppe de 36 000 USD/an structurée en trois fonds.

 

Objectif général de la mission est de produire deux (2) Manuels opérationnels complets, validés et prêts à

servir de documents de référence officiels pour la mise en œuvre des Microprojets (volet ndividus/coopératives

et volet PPP) et des Plateformes d'Innovation (13 PI) du ProAGRI, en pleine conformité avec les

réglementations fiduciaires et les Normes Environnementales et Sociales de la Banque mondiale.

Objectifs spécifiques

  1. Élaborer le Manuel opérationnel des Microprojets volet individus/coopératives couvrant l'ensemble du cycle — de l'appel à manifestation d'intérêt à la clôture des sous-projets — pour les ≈ 2 600 microprojets prévus dans les filières prioritaires du ProAGRI ;
  2. Élaborer le Manuel opérationnel des Microprojets volet PPP agro-industriels couvrant les critères de qualification des AIE, le processus de sélection et de négociation des conventions de PPP, les modalités de cofinancement (subvention ≤ 2 000 000 USD) et de décaissement conditionné aux résultats ;
  3. Élaborer le Manuel opérationnel des Plateformes d'Innovation pour les 13 PI du ProAGRI, en transformant la Note Conceptuelle existante pour les 9 PI maïs/sésame-arachide et en développant ex nihilo le cadre des 4 PI-poisson ;
  4. Garantir la cohérence interne des deux manuels et leur articulation avec les instruments complémentaires de la S/C 3.2 (Alliances Productives, warrantage, BDS, garantie IFC) ;
  5. Conduire les consultations multi-acteurs et animer les ateliers de validation nationaux, puis produire les versions finales des deux manuels pour approbation par l'UCP et non-objection de la Banque mondiale.

 

Le Ministère de la Production et de l’Industrialisation Agricole invite dès à présent les consultants individuels (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations sur leur capacité et expérience (curriculum vitae, lettre de motivation, attestations des services rendus, copies certifiées  des diplômes obtenus et autres supports) démontrant qu'ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations.

 

Les critères de sélection et les atouts sont les suivants :

 

  • Avoir un diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+5 minimum (Master, MBA, Ingénieur ou équivalent) en finance rurale, économie agricole, agroéconomie, développement rural, gestion de projets de développement ou domaine connexe avec spécialisation avérée en financement agricole.
  • Avoir au moins dix (10) ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente dans les domaines du financement agricole et rural (subventions, microprojets, matching grants, PPP agricoles), du développement des chaînes de valeur en Afrique subsaharienne, et de l'élaboration de manuels opérationnels ou de procédures pour des projets de développement financés par des bailleurs de fonds multilatéraux.
  • Avoir réalisé au minimum deux (2) missions d'élaboration ou de révision de manuels opérationnels
  • Avoir une expérience prouvée dans la conception ou la gestion de guichets de microprojets agricoles
  • Avoir participé à la conception ou à l'animation de Plateformes d'Innovation agricoles
  • Connaissance des filières maïs, arachide/sésame et/ou poisson
  • Maîtrise des règlements fiduciaires et des NES (normes 1 à 10) de la Banque mondiale applicables aux FPI ;

Atouts :

  • Maîtrise des outils de collecte numérique (KoboToolbox, ODK)
  • Connaissance du contexte institutionnel et agricole tchadien ou d'un pays sahélien à contexte similaire

 

NB : seules les expériences justifiées par des attestations de services faits seront prises en considération.

 

En cas d'ex-aequo, le volume des expériences pertinentes justifiées sera utilisé comme critère additionnel pour le classement final des consultants.

 

A l'issue de l'évaluation des manifestations d'intérêt, le consultant présentant le meilleur niveau de qualification et d'expérience en rapport avec la mission sera invité à négocier le contrat.

 

La durée totale de la mission est fixée à trois (3) mois, soit environ quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours calendaires. Cette durée tient compte du caractère exhaustif de l'inventaire attendu (nombre de magasins existants non précisément connu à ce stade), de l'étendue de la zone d'intervention du ProAGRI et du fait que la mission est confiée à un consultant individuel plutôt qu'à une équipe pluridisciplinaire.

 

Zone d'intervention : La mission se déroulera principalement à N'Djamena (siège de l'UCP). Des missions terrain sont prévues dans les agropoles (Moundou, Massakory, Abéché) et dans au moins une zone halieutique prioritaire. La logistique des déplacements sera organisée par l'UCP en concertation avec les UCR.

 

Le recrutement du consultant se fera suivant la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuels, avec une approche ouverte conformément au Règlement de passation des marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), révisé en Septembre 2025. Les candidats doivent être exempts de tout risque de conflits d’intérêt au regard des dispositions de l’article 3.16.d. et 3.22.d de ce Règlement.

 

Les expressions d’intérêt doivent être déposées sous pli fermé comprenant deux (02) exemplaires dont un original, tous placés dans une même enveloppe ou transmises par courrier électronique à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous, au plus tard le 18 septembre 2026 à 15 H 00 mn (TU + 1) et porter expressément la mention : A l’Attention du Coordonnateur National du ProAGRI : «Recrutement d'un consultant individuel International pour l’élaboration (i) du Manuel opérationnel de sélection et de subventionnement des Microprojets du ProAGRI — volet individus/coopératives et (ii) du Manuel opérationnel des Plateformes d'Innovation pour la mise en place et le financement des plans d'action de 13 PI (5 PI-maïs, 4 PI-arachide/sésame, 4 PI-poisson).

 

L’adresse de dépôt physique des manifestations d’intérêt est la suivante : UCP du ProAGRI, sise à l’Avenue Abbass Koty Yacoub, Quartier Farcha (à 300 m au Nord-Est de ORCA) ;

 

L’adresse de dépôt par voie électronique est la suivante : proagritchad@outlook.com;  abdallahgoroumimahamat@gmail.com;  mhtnaim61@gmail.com

 

 

Le Secrétaire Général du Ministère de la Production

              et de l’Industrialisation Agricole

 

 

 MOUBARACK ABAKAR ROUBO

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(FRAMEWORK AGREEMENTS FOR CONSULTING SERVICES )

 

Lebanese Republic

Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR)

Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP)

Loan No: __ IBRD-98410

Procurement Reference: FA-CS-ESIA-ESMP

Assignment Title: Framework Agreements for the Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMP), and Environmental and Social Audits (ESA).

 

The Lebanese Republic (hereinafter called the “Borrower”) has received financing in the amount of US$250 million from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) (the “Bank”) toward the cost of the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP). The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), acting as the executing agency on behalf of the Government of Lebanon, intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under contracts for consulting services under Framework Agreements.

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve engaging qualified Environmental and Social consulting firms under Framework Agreements to provide environmental and social assessment services, including the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), and Environmental and Social Audits (ESAs), for infrastructure and public service projects financed under the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP). The Framework Agreements will be concluded through a Two-Stage Selection Process and the consulting services shall include the preparation of:

  • Module 1: Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) Checklist (Low-Risk Subprojects);
  • Module 2: Site-Specific Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs);
  • Module 3: Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), including Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs);
  • Module 4: Environmental and Social Audits (ESAs), including Environmental and Social Action Plans (ESAPs) for Existing Facilities.

Specific Call-Off Contracts will be issued, on an as-needed basis, depending on the environmental and social risk classification of each activity in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF). The Framework Agreement(s) shall be signed for a duration of Thirty-Six (36) months with one or more qualified consulting firms. Individual assignments shall subsequently be awarded through Call-Off competitions among Framework Agreement holders.

The full version of the Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found on the CDR website at: https://www.cdr.gov.lb/Procurement.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultant Brochures may also be included in the submission. The shortlisting criteria are:

1. Firm Legal Standing & Core Buisness and Years of Experience

  • Legal registration and authorization to operate in its country of incorporation, demonstrating financial soundness.
  • Legally established consulting firm (or lead member of a Joint Venture of maximum two (2) members) with a minimum of eight (8) years of demonstrated experience in environmental and social assessment services for infrastructure and public service projects.

2. Specific Technical Experience

The Consultant shall demonstrate the following with submission of list of activities that best demonstrate the following experiences:

  • Experience in the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) and, where applicable, Environmental and Social Audits (ESAs) for infrastructure and public service projects.
  • Experience in the application of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including the preparation of environmental and social instruments in accordance with the applicable Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), and the World Bank Group Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines, preferably under projects financed by International Financial Institutions is considered as an advantage.
  • Familiarity with the Lebanese environmental regulatory framework, including Environmental Impact Assessment Decree No. 8633/2012 and other applicable environmental legislation and regulations is considered as an advantage.
  • The introduced list of experiences could include: Experience in identifying, assessing and developing mitigation measures for environmental and social risks and impacts associated with infrastructure and public service projects, including, as applicable:
    • Labor and Working Conditions;
    • Occupational Health and Safety (OHS);
    • Community Health and Safety;
    • Land Acquisition and Involuntary Resettlement;
    • Biodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Management of Living Natural Resources;
    • Cultural Heritage;
    • Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA), and Sexual Harassment (SH).
  • Experience in environmental and social assessment of reconstruction, rehabilitation and/or post-conflict infrastructure projects will be considered an asset.

3. Technical and Managerial Capacity and a general Quality Management Submission of a Quality Management Approach (maximum ten (10) pages) describing the firm's standard procedures, methodologies and quality assurance mechanisms for the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), and Environmental and Social Audits (ESAs). No project-specific methodology or pricing is required at this stage.

  • Submission of a list of professional staff available to the consultant firm.

The EOI submission shall be limited to a maximum of twenty-five (25) pages maximum.

Please note that at this shortlisting stage:

  • Technical and financial proposals are not requested.
  • Key Experts, if proposed for the assignment, will not be evaluated.
  • Requests for clarification on the REOI or TOR may not be replied to at this time, as the allocated time for submission of EOI does not permit such exchanges.

The shortlist shall comprise five (5) to eight (8) consulting firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting Services and Consulting Services, dated February 2025, setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a Joint Venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected.

Shortlisted Consultants will subsequently be invited to submit proposals under the Framework Agreement selection process in accordance with the Least Cost Selection method described in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (February 2025).

The deadline for receiving Expressions of Interest shall be by Friday, September 11th, 2026 at 12:00 noon Beirut local time.

Expressions of Interest (EOI) shall be delivered to the address below by hand or courier, including one (1) original, one (1) copy and one (1) electronic copy on CD-ROM.

PROGRAMA DE SUSTENTABILIDADE FISCAL, EFICIÊNCIA E EFICÁCIA DO GASTO PÚBLICO – PROGESTÃO RS SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE – SMI – Nº 004/PROGESTÃO/RS/2026 AVISO DE SELEÇÃO DE CONSULTOR INDIVIDUAL (CI)

Processo administrativo: 26/1300-9002416-8

A Comissão Especial de Licitações – CEL do PROGESTÃO RS, designada pela Portaria SPGG nº 59/2026, torna pública a presente Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse – SMI, destinada à seleção de Consultor Individual para a prestação dos serviços descritos neste Aviso e no respectivo Termo de Referência, no âmbito do Programa de Sustentabilidade Fiscal, Eficiência e Eficácia do Gasto Público do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul – PROGESTÃO RS.

1. Contexto do PROGESTÃO RS O Programa de Sustentabilidade Fiscal, Eficiência e Eficácia do Gasto Público do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul – PROGESTÃO RS, é uma iniciativa do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul, regulamentada pelo Decreto nº 58.647, de 3 de março de 2026, e financiada pelo Banco Internacional para Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento – BIRD/Banco Mundial, por meio do Acordo de Empréstimo nº 9787-BR. O Programa tem por finalidade aprimorar a gestão pública estadual e promover maior eficiência e eficácia do gasto público, por meio de ações de caráter multissetorial voltadas, entre outras áreas, à gestão fiscal, financeira e patrimonial, à modernização das compras públicas e ao fortalecimento da capacidade institucional do Estado. As aquisições e contratações realizadas no âmbito do PROGESTÃO RS observam também os princípios de Value for Money (VfM), economia, integridade, adequação à finalidade, eficiência, transparência e equidade, de modo a assegurar processos competitivos, transparentes e alinhados aos objetivos de desenvolvimento do Programa.

2. Objeto da Contratação Contratação de serviços de consultoria individual para ministrar capacitação em análise custo-benefício de projetos de investimentos públicos. O Termo de Referência – TDR, contendo o detalhamento do objeto e demais condições da contratação, integra esta Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse como Anexo I.

3. Método de Seleção A seleção será realizada mediante comparação das qualificações e experiências de, pelo menos, três Consultores Individuais qualificados para a execução dos serviços, sempre que disponíveis, sendo selecionado o candidato mais bem avaliado segundo os critérios estabelecidos no Termo de Referência. O Consultor que obtiver a melhor avaliação será convidado para a etapa de negociação, conforme os procedimentos aplicáveis. A apresentação de Manifestação de Interesse não gera direito à contratação nem obrigação de contratação por parte do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul.

4. Instruções para Submissão e Contatos Interessados em participar da seleção deverão formalizar sua Manifestação de Interesse e encaminhar, juntamente com ela, os documentos comprobatórios necessários à demonstração de sua qualificação e experiência para a execução do objeto. A documentação deverá ser enviada exclusivamente por meio eletrônico, em formato PDF, para o endereço celprogestao@spgg.rs.gov.br, devendo constar no campo “Assunto” a identificação “SMI – 004/2026”. O prazo limite para o recebimento das Manifestações de Interesse é 22 de setembro de 2026. Esclarecimentos sobre esta seleção podem ser obtidos por meio do e-mail supramencionado. As informações adicionais e o progresso do processo seletivo estarão disponíveis no site da CELIC: https://celic.rs.gov.br/progestao-rs.

Porto Alegre, RS, 04 de setembro de 2026.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

Consulting Services – Firm Selection

Project: Digital Skilling for Employment (DSE) Project
Assignment: Penetration Testing and Security & Data-Protection Compliance Assessment – nammiskills Platform V2
Reference No.: LB-FORWARDMENA-541113-CS-CQS
Selection Method: Consultant’s Qualifications-based Selection (CQS)

The Digital Skilling for Employment (DSE) Project is financed by the Kingdom of the Netherlands under the PROSPECTS Partnership and administered by the World Bank. The Project aims to increase access to market-relevant digital skills and income-generating opportunities for vulnerable youth in Lebanon.

As part of the Project, Forward Digital MENA operates nammiskills, a multilingual digital platform supporting learners in assessing their skills, identifying career pathways, accessing learning opportunities, and connecting to employment opportunities.

Scope of the Assignment:

Forward Digital MENA intends to engage an independent cybersecurity consulting firm to conduct penetration testing and a security and data-protection compliance assessment of nammiskills V2.

The assignment will cover, among other areas, the platform's web application, APIs, cloud environment, authentication and access controls, multi-tenant architecture, AI/LLM interfaces, third-party integrations, data-protection controls, remediation verification and retesting.

Minimum Qualifications

Interested firms should demonstrate:

  • Proven experience in penetration testing and security assessments of web applications, APIs and cloud-hosted platforms.
  • Successful completion of at least two (2) comparable assignments within the last five (5) years, preferably involving personal data, multi-tenant systems, GDPR or equivalent data-protection requirements.
  • Relevant cybersecurity certifications or accreditations such as CREST, ISO/IEC 27001 or equivalent will be considered an advantage.
  • Availability of suitably qualified expertise in penetration testing, application/API security, data protection/GDPR and AWS/cloud security.

The selected Consultant must remain independent from the company responsible for the design, development, implementation or maintenance of nammiskills V2 and will be required to sign a Declaration of Independence and Absence of Conflict of Interest at contract signature.

Request for the Terms of Reference

Interested eligible consulting firms are invited to request the complete Terms of Reference (TOR) by email at:

michelle@forwardmena.org

Subject: Request for TOR – Cybersecurity Assessment of nammiskills Platform V2 – LB-FORWARDMENA-541113-CS-CQS

The complete TOR, including the detailed scope of work, deliverables, qualification requirements, proposal submission requirements and applicable deadlines, will be provided to interested eligible firms upon receipt of their request.

Selection Method

The Consultant will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method in accordance with the applicable World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Submission

Interested firms shall submit their proposals in accordance with the requirements and instructions provided in the TOR.

Proposal submission deadline: 04 September 2026 at 17:00 Beirut Time.

Requests for clarification shall be submitted in writing in accordance with the instructions provided in the TOR.

SUIVI ET CONTRÔLE DES TRAVAUX I) DE RÉALISATION DE DIX (10) SYSTÈMES MULTI-VILLAGES D’ALIMENTATION EN EAU POTABLE DANS LA ZONE NORD DE LA CÔTE D’IVOIRE, II) D’ALIMENTATION EN EAU POTABLE DE SOBA ET LES LOCALITÉS ENVIRONNANTES DE FROTOTOU ET KOMATOU (S/P KANI)
