REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Mongolia

Name of Project: Fourth Energy Sector Project (P509161)

IBRD Loan No.: 9873-MN

Assignment Title: Employer’s Technical Supervision

Reference No: MN-MOE-ESP4-3-CS-QCBS

 

The Government of Mongolia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Fourth Energy Sector Project (P509161) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) will provide Employer’s Technical Supervision services for the design, construction, installation, testing, commissioning, handover, and Defects Notification Period of the Mandalgobi – Arvaikheer 220 kV transmission line and associated substation  works, to be implemented under multiple contract lots, in ensuring compliance with contractual requirements, applicable laws and legislation of Mongolia, and the World Bank Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), including relevant Quality standards and environmental, social, health and safety (ESHS) standards. The Services shall cover all phases of the Project lifecycle.

The assignment duration shall be thirty-six (36) months, comprising approximately: (i) twenty-four (24) months for design review, construction supervision, testing and commissioning, and support to the Employer up to the issuance of the Taking-Over Certificate (TOC); and (ii) twelve (12) months of Defects Notification Period support on an oncall basis.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for assignment can be found at:

           https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dGjcHPrmfl4bQQEB4LlzhboAafIhPHlO/view?usp=sharing

The Ministry of Energy now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the Services, including:

  • Relevant experience in assignments of similar nature, scope, and complexity, particularly technical supervision for high-voltage transmission lines and substations and under comparable conditions (e.g., similar countries, sectors, climate conditions, or project environments);
  • Firm’s core business, years in operation, and technical and managerial capabilities relevant to the assignment;
  • Organizational capacity, availability of qualified personnel, quality monitoring approaches, and resources;
  • Supporting documentation, as appropriate.

 

Shortlisting criteria are as follows:

The Consultant shall have proven experience in supervising of high-voltage transmission lines and substations (220 kV and above), FIDIC-based contract administration, and preferably World Bank-financed projects.

  • At least seven (7) years of experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity in the energy sector, particularly in transmission network expansion;
  • Proven experience in successfully completing at least one (1) technical supervision assignment for high-voltage transmission lines and substations (220 kV and above) preferably in countries with similar climatic conditions;
  • Experience working with government agencies and international financial institutions (IFIs) is an advantage;
  • Demonstrated organizational capacity, including strong technical and managerial capability, and effective management, coordination, and quality assurance arrangements.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualification, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. Only selected firm through this expression of interest process will be invited to submit a technical and financial proposal.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by e-mail at dulguun@energy.gov.mn no later than 10:00 a.m. (local time) on 2 October 2026.

procnotices.notice_text:
MINISTERE DE L’AGRICULTURE ET DE LA SOUVERAINETE ALIMENTAIRE

----------

SECRETARIAT GENERAL

---

PROJET DE RESILIENCE DES SYSTEMES ALIMENTAIRES DE MADAGASCAR (FSRP)

----------

Crédit IDA-71570-MG/Don IDA-E0830-MG – Madagascar - PPM STEP N° CI 16-26/CN

----------

SELECTION DE CONSULTANTS PAR LES EMPRUNTEURS DE LA BANQUE MONDIALE

APPEL A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET N° CI 16-26/CN

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL RESPONSABLE EN EAU ET IRRIGATION AU NIVEAU DE L’UNITE D’EXECUTION INTER REGIONALE ATSINANANA DU FSRP

(RELANCE)

Poste basé à Toamasina

  1. La République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque Mondiale pour couvrir le coût du PROJET DE RESILIENCE DES SYSTEMES ALIMENTAIRES DE MADAGASCAR (FSRP) sous tutelle du Ministère de l’Agriculture et de la souveraineté alimentaire (MiASA), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit/don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL RESPONSABLE EN EAU ET IRRIGATION AU NIVEAU DE L’UNITE D’EXECUTION INTER REGIONALE ATSINANANA DU PROJET DE RESILIENCE DES SYSTEMES ALIMENTAIRES DE MADAGASCAR (RELANCE) , Postes basés à Toamasina »
  2. Les services de consultant individuel (« les services ») consistent à contribuer à la bonne marche et à la réalisation des activités du projet, relatives à la gestion efficace des ressources en eau et des infrastructures hydroagricoles, la réduction de l'érosion, et l'amélioration de la productivité agricole ainsi que de leur suivi et évaluation principalement pour les activités liées à la Composante 2 au niveau de son unité régionale. Le Consultant est placé sous la supervision directe du Coordonnateur Régional et est en collaboration fonctionnelle et opérationnelle avec l’Unité de Gestion du Projet, en particulier le Responsable Eau et Irrigation National.
  3. Le contrat durera jusqu’à la fin du Projet le 30 juin 2029, avec une période d’essai de trois (03) mois la première année. Le renouvellement du contrat chaque année est conditionné par la remise des rapports précisés au point 6 des termes de référence, ainsi que par les résultats d'une évaluation de performance satisfaisante par le Projet et l’Administration.

Les termes de référence détaillés (TdR) pour la mission et le modèle de CV peuvent être obtenus aux adresses indiquées ci-dessous.

  1. L’Unité de Gestion du PROJET DE RESILIENCE DES SYSTEMES ALIMENTAIRES DE MADAGASCAR (FSRP) invite maintenant les consultants individuels éligibles ("Consultants individuels") à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants individuels intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services, et constituer un dossier de manifestation d’intérêt incluant :
  • Une lettre de motivation rédigée en français ;
  • Un CV détaillé ;
  • Un CV selon le canevas annexé aux termes de référence ;
  • Les copies des diplômes certifiées par l’Etablissement universitaire ;
  • Attestations de travail pour justifier les expériences ;
  • Une adresse email et un numéro de téléphone pour contact rapide.
  1. Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :
  • Ingénieur du Génie Rural ou hydraulicien, de niveau BAC+5 au minimum,
  • Ayant au moins dix (10) années d’expérience professionnelle générale.  Il a au moins cinq (05) années d’expérience dans le domaine des études et travaux liées à des programmes de réhabilitation des périmètres irrigués. Il devra justifier d’une bonne connaissance des contraintes spécifiques des réseaux hydro agricoles, et des suivis des travaux d’infrastructure de Génie civil et Génie rural, et également des problématiques liées à la gestion de l’eau et aux Associations des Usagers de l’Eau
  • Ayant participé à des études (au moins à deux (02) missions) et à la supervision des travaux de réhabilitation ou d’aménagement de périmètres irrigués (au moins à deux (02) missions), en tant qu’Ingénieur d’études ou de surveillance, sinon plus (chef de mission, ingénieur de contrôle). – OU - ayant participé au moins à deux (02) missions similaires en tant que Responsable Eau et Irrigation régional d’un projet financé par la Banque mondiale, dans les zones tropicales et subsahariennes serait un atout majeur,
  • Posséder des expériences en gestion et en planification dans le domaine des infrastructures au sein des projets de développement rural similaire au projet,
  • Maitrise des procédures de passations de marché et sauvegarde environnementale et sociale de la Banque Mondiale,
  • Ayant une bonne connaissance et une expérience pratique en matière institutionnelle, juridique et réglementaire concernant la mise en place et l’appui aux Associations d’usagers de l’eau pour la gestion et l’entretien des réseaux, et ayant participé à au moins deux (02) missions de mise en place et d’appui aux Associations d’usagers de l’eau
  • Maitrise des logiciels de conceptions assistées par ordinateur (Autocad), SIG
  • Des expériences en réhabilitation/maintenance de réseaux hydroagricole (études et conduite de travaux) dans les zones du projet sont très souhaitées,
  • Apte à faire des fréquents déplacements dans les régions du projet et à des déplacements en moto, en canot dans les zones du projet.
  • Disposé à travailler au sein d’une équipe multidisciplinaire, et apte à travailler sous pression,
  • Présentant une bonne intégrité, Bonne conduite et professionnalisme (aucune antécédant au mauvais comportement relatif aux VBG et harcèlement sexuel, racismes, corruptions)
  • Ayant une capacité justifiée en rédaction de rapport en langue Française, et Malagasy,
  • Une bonne connaissance / compréhension de l’anglais constitue un atout.
  1. L'attention des Consultants individuels intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI », 7ème édition, Septembre 2025, énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.
  2. Un consultant individuel sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de sélection agréée pour les Consultants Individuels énoncée dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.
  3. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau de 08h30 à 16h30.
  4. Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être remises par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (physique et/ou électronique en version word et pdf), sous enveloppe fermée mentionnant clairement sur l’enveloppe extérieure et dans l’objet de l’email le nom du poste au plus tard le 18 Septembre 2026 à 16 h 00 (heure locale).
  5.  Adresses auxquelles il est fait référence ci-dessus :
  • Bureau du Projet de Résilience des Systèmes Alimentaires de Madagascar (FSRP), à la Direction du Génie Rural Nanisana, Enceinte ex-BVPI- Antananarivo 101 - Madagascar
  • Tél : +261 38 74 129 19
  • Emails : passation.fsrp@gmail.com; cc : rpm.fsrp23@gmail.com , spmvola.fsrp@gmail.com, apmantsa.fsrp@gmail.com

Antananarivo, le 04 Septembre 2026

Le Coordonnateur National,

RAFALIMANANA Oliva

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

UKRAINE

Country: Ukraine

Program: «Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program»

Grant : TF0C5794

Project : P504171

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Development of Model Programs for Professionally Oriented Specialised Secondary Education

Contract Package ID: LEARN-1.1-CIRRICULA

Ukraine has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program.

The Ministry of Education and Science intends to use part of the proceeds for consulting services, for which this REoI has been issued.

Consulting services (hereinafter referred to as "Services") include: supporting MoES in developing a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

The expected period for the Consultant to provide services for the development of the online course is approximately 6 calendar months, starting in December 2026.

Detailed information regarding the provision of the specified Services is provided in the Terms of Reference (hereinafter referred to as "TOR"), which is attached.

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (hereinafter referred to as the "Client") invites qualified consulting companies (hereinafter referred to as "Consultants") to express their interest in providing the specified Services. Interested Consultants must provide information that confirms their qualifications and experience required to perform the Services.

The evaluation of the expressions of interest provided by the Consultants will be carried out based on the following criteria:

Minimum Qualification Requirements (Pass/Fail Basis)

Failure to meet any of the requirements below shall result in disqualification.

Core Business and Experience

  • At least 3 (three) years of experience in education, curriculum development, institutional development, or related fields;
  • At least 3 (three) successfully completed assignments during the last 6 years in one or more of the following areas:

–       curriculum development or educational program design;

–       vocational education or education sector projects;

–       capacity building programs for education institutions.

In case of a Joint Venture / Consortium (JVCA), the Lead Member shall demonstrate substantial compliance with the above requirements, including at least 3 (three) years of relevant experience and participation in at least 2 (two) relevant assignments. The JVCA as a whole must meet all qualification requirements.

Financial Capacity

  • Average annual turnover for the last 3 completed financial years shall be at least USD 150,000 or equivalent.

 In case of a JVCA: Lead Member: minimum 50% of the annual turnover requirement; Other members: minimum 25% of the annual turnover requirement; Combined: must fully meet the annual turnover requirement. Audited financial statements or verified financial documents shall be provided.

Experience with Donor-Funded Projects

  • At least one assignment financed by international financial institutions or bilateral donors (e.g., World Bank, EBRD, EU, GIZ, UNICEF, etc.) within the last 5 years is an advantage.

Staff

The Consultant shall provide suitably qualified professionals in terms of expertise and time allocation to complete the activities required under the scope of work and to finally achieve the objectives of the Assignment in terms of time, costs and quality, within the agreed timeframe.

The Consultant shall also provide adequate administrative staff (secretaries, translators, etc.) needed to support the expert team.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, items 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers[1], dated September 2023 with amendments of September 2025[2] (hereinafter referred to as the "Procurement Regulations"), which contains the World Bank's policy regarding conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

Selection of a Consultant will be performed in accordance with Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection (CQS) method following World Bank’s Consultants Guidelines.

Further information may be obtained at the address below.

Expressions of interest must be submitted in Ukrainian or English via email to the address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org; uiherp@mon.gov.ua by 2:00 PM Kyiv time on September 30, 2026.[3]

Expressions of interest to be clearly marked: "LEARN-1.1-CIRRICULA: Expression of Interest".

Consultants should provide not only information demonstrating their compliance with the Mandatory Minimum Qualification Requirements, but also information that meets the specific requirements of the assignment and will be considered an advantage. The Consultant rating will be based on compliance with these latter requirements. The Consultant with the highest rating, determined according to the established criteria for evaluating the Consultant’s qualifications, will be invited to submit a technical and financial proposal.

Information on the Consultant’s experience provided by the Consultants must be documented (copies of contracts or parts thereof, and acceptance certificates for services provided; additionally, client references may be submitted, describing the specifics of the completed assignment).

Interested Consultants are additionally advised to pay attention to the following aspects when preparing their information:

  • Files submitted by the Consultant should be in PDF (Portable Document Format) and/or JPG formats and should be as consolidated as possible;
  • When preparing information describing your qualifications and experience, provide as much detail as possible to demonstrate compliance with the established qualification criteria and relevance to the assignment;
  • Include copies of documents confirming the stated experience and competencies, and provide contact information of third parties who can confirm your experience and provide relevant references.

Consultants who have submitted an EOI should not submit any documents or information after the deadline for EOI submission, except for providing documents and/or information requested by the Employer for clarification or explanation of the submitted EOI. Any exchange of information between the Employer and Consultants must be in writing via the official email addresses specified in this announcement.

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School”” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$451 million provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) and Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at aligning the education system with labour market needs, supporting economic recovery, and advancing Ukraine’s European integration agenda.

A key component of this reform is the introduction of professionally oriented upper secondary education, which integrates general education with early professional orientation and creates structured pathways between general secondary education, vocational education, and professional pre-higher education.

The regulatory and methodological framework required for this transformation has already been established, including:

  • adoption of the Law of Ukraine “On professional (vocational) education” (August 2025);
  • development of secondary legislation and regulatory acts;
  • approval of competency-based professional education standards;
  • entry into force of the State Standard of Specialised Secondary Education (Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated July 25, 2024 No. 851);
  • Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 08.06.2026 no. 898);
  • Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine No. 675 dated 05.06.2023

 

Initial experience in developing model programs has demonstrated strong demand, high institutional interest, and significant scalability potential. At the same time, the system currently lacks a sufficient number of professionally oriented model programs across priority economic sectors, as well as adapted academic content aligned with professional pathways.

Given that the regulatory framework has only recently been finalised, this Assignment represents the first opportunity to implement curriculum transformation at scale within a fully operational legal and methodological environment.

Under the GPE-financed institutional capacity activities, MoES intends to engage a qualified Consultant to develop a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education. The Assignment shall be implemented over a period of six (6) months from the Effective Date of the Contract. The Assignment will enable rapid, scalable transformation of curriculum content, directly impacting over 37,000 learners in priority economic sectors and creating a foundation for nationwide implementation of professionally oriented upper secondary education.

 

The Assignment is expected to be implemented in line with World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and applicable Ukrainian legislation.

 

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of the Assignment is to support MoES in developing a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

Specifically, the Assignment is to develop forty-one (41) model programs of mandatory educational components by educational domains for four (4) specializations of professionally oriented specialised secondary education, namely, Construction, Engineering and Technology, Information Technology, and Medical specialization (aligned with priority economic sectors) under the State standard of profile secondary education.

The model programs should be aligned with professional standards, labour market needs and sectoral requirements, as well as provide a unified national approach to curriculum development and adaptation.

The Consultant shall achieve the above objective in full compliance with applicable regulatory and legal framework of Ukraine, including relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, and procurement and implementation requirements of the World Bank.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

3.1 Overall Approach

The Consultant shall provide comprehensive technical, methodological and organisational support to MoES for the development of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

The Assignment shall build upon the existing regulatory framework developed by MoES.

The implementation logic shall follow a structured sequence:

  1. Mobilisation of the expert pool.
  2. Development of specialised model programs.
  3. Quality assurance and validation.

All activities shall ensure consistency, scalability, and alignment across programs.

3.2 Components

Component 1. Expert Mobilisation and Coordination

The Consultant shall mobilise and manage a structured expert pool and ensure effective coordination throughout all stages of the Assignment.

The Consultant shall:

  • mobilise and manage a structured expert pool including:
    • VE and PPHE educators;
    • scientific and research-pedagogical staff (academics involved in relevant fields of study); 
    • sectoral experts from industry;
    • methodological specialists from NMCs;
  • ensure balanced representation across sectors;
  • establish coordination mechanisms and workflows;
  • assign clear roles and responsibilities;
  • develop Quality Assurance Plan;
  • ensure timely delivery of outputs.

It is recommended that each Model Program draft be developed by a compact drafting team comprising at least two (2) Subject Experts (Non-Key Experts) responsible for its development.

Each Sectoral Expert shall coordinate all drafts of Model Programs  within the assigned specialization and responsible for:

  • methodological supervision;
  • coordination of drafting teams;
  • ensuring consistency across all Model Programs within the specialization;
  • ensuring compliance with the State Standard of Specialized Secondary Education, the Typical Educational Program and methodological guidance approved by MoES;
  • internal quality control before submission for independent review.

Subject Experts may contribute to the development of more than one Model Program draft depending on their qualifications and the implementation methodology proposed by the Consultant.

All experts shall be engaged on a contractual basis, with clearly defined deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations.

Component 2. Development of Specialised Model Programs

The Consultant shall develop forty-one (41) specialised model programs across four (4) specializations defined according to priority economic sectors in accordance with State standard of specialised secondary education, Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation and Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums.The four priority sectors are:

    • Construction;
    • Engineering and technology;
    • Information technology;
    • Medical

Each program shall:

  • integrate general education subjects into applied, sector-specific contexts;
  • align with professional standards and occupational requirements;
  • reflect labour market needs;
  • follow State standard of specialised secondary education and Typical educational program of specialised secondary education;
  • be developed in accordance with the academic integrity values.

The development of every model program draft shall be based on the Typical educational programme for professionally oriented specialised secondary education approved under Order 898 and on the corresponding Typical curriculum plan for each of the four profiles listed above. The list of mandatory educational components for which MPs shall be developed for each profile, together with the corresponding number of teaching hours, hours of independent work, ECTS credits and their distribution between the profile-adaptation cycle (year 1) and the profile cycle (years 2-3), is set out in Annex 1 to this ToR.

 

Each MP shall comply with the structure and content requirements established in the Typical Educational Programme and shall consist, at minimum, of the following four parts:

  • Title page – name of the ministry/institution; type of programme (model programme / programme based on a model programme / programme not based on a model programme); type of mandatory educational component (subject, discipline, integrated/crosssectoral/special course, module, etc.); programme title; education level; profile of study; educational domain(s); assessment benchmarks (basic or advanced); author(s); year of development;
  • Introductory part – author's concept and the role and significance of the component; relevance for the selected profile; aim and objectives aligned with the assessment benchmarks of the State Standard and with the chosen profile; references to the relevant educational domain(s) and to professional standards, occupational qualification characteristics or professional prehigher education standards used as a basis; crossreferences to other MPs jointly covering the same mandatory learning outcomes, where applicable; workload in hours and ECTS credits; structural elements; recommended forms of organising the educational process;
  • Main part – titles and workload in hours of structural elements (content lines, sections, topics); expected learning outcomes linked to, and retaining the indexation of, the mandatory learning outcomes of the State Standard; proposed content reflecting professionally oriented, sectorspecific contexts relevant to the profile; recommended learning activities and active/interactive forms of organising learning; recommended methodological support bearing the "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" grif;
  • Concluding part – strategy and methodological recommendations for achieving the expected learning outcomes; description of assessment tools and instruments; reference to possible alternative assessment systems.

 

Each MP shall be submitted in the following format: paper size A4 (210×297 mm); font Times New Roman; main text – 14 pt; tables, footnotes and supplementary text – 10–12 pt; line spacing – 1.0; continuous page numbering starting from the second page.

The total workload of each MP, expressed in hours and ECTS credits, shall correspond exactly to the figures established for the relevant educational component for the respective profile, as set out in Annex 1. Any deviation shall be justified in writing by the Consultant and shall require prior written approval by MoES.

Although the educational domains of the components listed in Annexes 1 are common to all profiles, the content of each MP shall be professionally oriented to the specific profile for which it is developed, in accordance with Section 4 of the Typical Educational Programme. In particular, each MP shall:

  • integrate the competency potential and core knowledge of the relevant educational domain(s), as defined by the State Standard, with applied, occupation specific contexts relevant to the profile;
  • be consistent with the values, cross cutting skills and recommended forms of learning activity described in the Typical educational rogramme.

The development cycle shall be completed within 90 working days.

Considering the large number of tasks included under this component, it may be practical to divide it into two implementation stages.

In accordance with the Quality Assurance Plan and MoES regulations the Consultant shall ensure the quality of all specialised model programs developed under this Assignment through a two-tier quality assurance system: (i) the Consultant's own internal quality assurance process, and (ii) the official State expertise and grif procedure administered by MoES and  in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes (MoES Order No. 675 of 5 June 2023).

Tier 1 - Consultant's internal quality assurance

The Consultant shall:

  • conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle;
  • ensure consistency of outputs across all profiles through centralised coordination by the Quality Assurance Expert;
  • develop all the outputs following the academic integrity values

The Consultant may conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle and/or organise independent blind peer review as part of the Consultant’s internal quality assurance processes.

Tier 2 - Submission for the official MoES grif procedure

Each MP shall be submitted by the Consultant, through MoES to Ukrainian Institute of Education Development for expertise and the grant of the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine," in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes.

The Consultant shall note that, pursuant to paragraph 6 of Section IV of the Procedure, expertise of model programmes (as objects falling under subparagraph 3 of paragraph 5 of Section I of the Procedure) is exempt from the standard fee-based expertise mechanism. The Consultant's budget shall accordingly cover only its own internal quality assurance activity.

 Expertise process and timelines to be reflected in the Work Schedule

The Consultant's Work Schedule shall account for the following parameters of the official procedure:

  • expertise is conducted by at least two members of the relevant Commission and/or expert group, selected by a method of random selection with regard to their professional background, specialisation and place of work;
  • the Commission's reasoned expert opinion is to be expected within two months of submission, unless a different period is agreed;
  • where the Commission requires revision, the Consultant shall resubmit the revised MP together with a reasoned response to each comment within 30 calendar days of receipt of the extract from the Commission's protocol;
  • the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" is granted by MoES order and is valid for five years, expiring on 1 July of the relevant year;
  • upon granting of the grif, the MP is entered in the public Catalogue of Granted Grifs maintained by MoES and the Institution.

The Assignment shall be deemed complete in respect of Component 2 only once the full package of drafts of model programs has obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue, once each tranche of programs has obtained such confirmation. Evidence of the grant of the grif and of the Catalogue entry shall be annexed to the relevant Interim or Final Completion Report.

Deliverable 4. Final Completion Report

The following outputs shall be delivered under this deliverable and documented in the Final Completion Report:

  • lessons learned and next steps for further implementation.

The Consultant shall submit a Draft Final Completion Report no later than one month before the completion of the Assignment, summarising overall implementation results, achievement of objectives and targets, key lessons learned, and recommendations for further institutionalisation and sustainability.

Reports Submission and Acceptance Procedure

The following procedure shall apply to all reports submitted under this Assignment: the Inception Report (Deliverable 1), Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs (Deliverable 2), and Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs (Deliverable 3) and the Final Completion Report (Deliverable 4).

The exact format of the reports will be discussed and agreed upon with MoES and, where applicable, with the World Bank, upon contract signing and before the commencement of the Assignment. All reports and deliverables will be submitted in a minimum of two (2) hard copies in English and two (2) hard copies in Ukrainian. The products developed (model programs as well as methodological materials for development for Ukrainian-speaking users) shall be submitted in Ukrainian only, without translation, and included as annexes to the relevant reports. All materials developed under this Assignment shall become the property of MoES.

The Consultant shall submit:

  • the draft version of the Inception Report – within 20 calendar days from the Effective Date;
  • the draft version of Interim Report on development of the 1st set of Specialised Model Programs – no later than the 14th calendar day after completing the delivery of Component 2 activities according to the Work Schedule;
  • the draft version of Interim Report on development of the 2nd set of Specialised Model Programs  – no later than the 14th calendar day after completing the delivery of Component 2 activities according to the Work Schedule;
  • the draft version of the Final Report – at latest 30 calendar days before the completion of the services.

The draft of each report shall be submitted in electronic (Word/Excel and PDF) format to the Client’s email address specified in the Contract. The Client will review the draft within 14 calendar days from the date of receipt and provide comments, or confirm the quality and correspondence of the Assignment with the requirements of these Terms of Reference. The Consultant, within 7 calendar days from receipt of comments, shall process them and submit the revised report in electronic and paper format, together with a table indicating, for each comment, the method of its consideration or justification for any deviation.

If the Client has no comments on the revised report, the report shall be deemed approved, which shall be confirmed by a signed Acceptance Certificate for Services. If the Client does not respond with comments within the above-mentioned period, the draft report shall be deemed accepted.

If required by MoES, the Consultant shall provide ad-hoc reports within 3–7 calendar days, depending on the complexity of the request.

procnotices.notice_text:
GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

 

BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA

AGRICULTURE RESILIENCE AND COMPETITIVENESS PROJECT

Project ID No. P171266

 

LOAN NO. 9359-BA

 

 

The Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina has received financing in the amount of US$ 80.0 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Agriculture Resilience and Competitiveness Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project.

 

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to increase climate resilience and competitiveness of the agriculture sector.

 

The project will include the following components:

 

  1. Component 1: Enhancing Public Support Resilience and Traceability.

 

(a)       Enhancing agriculture information systems, through, inter alia: (i) enhancement of the farm and client register, including establishing new registers, information systems and web portals, as might be necessary; (ii) development of a payment system; (iii) strengthening the existing agricultural information system; and (iv) establishment of the Farm Accountancy Data Network;

(b)       Supporting climate-resilient agriculture, through, inter alia: (i) improvement of seed quality and production, (ii) activities to increase farmers’ awareness of possible climate change impacts; and (iii) improvement of extension services delivery, including through developing of related information systems, registers and web portals, as well as providing support to producers to comply with good agricultural practices, integrated pest management and climate risk assessment and interventions in value chains;

(c)       Enhancing agriculture information system’s capacities for the benefit of MoFTER.

 

  1. Component 2: Improving Agriculture Productivity, Adaptation to Climate Change, and Enhancing Linkages with Markets.

 

(a)       Strengthening value chains and developing productive partnerships through: (i) provision of Matching Grants to eligible Beneficiaries for carrying out Matching Grant Subprojects with the aim to support: input supply, marketing of horticulture and livestock products in the internal and external markets, and increase of knowledge and capacity of the Beneficiaries; (ii) technical assistance to the Beneficiaries to comply with the market requirements; and (iii) awareness activities to promote the Matching Grants.

 

(b)       Improving irrigation and drainage systems for climate change adaptation Sub-projects, including: (i) construction of new, and rehabilitation and modernization of selected existing irrigation and drainage systems, including the preparation of the feasibility and design studies; and (ii) strengthening of irrigation and drainage management institutions, including capacity building of selected local administrative bodies, WUAs and local utility companies, development of a database of all irrigation systems and assessment of their functionalities, and development of the drainage information management system.

 

  1. Component 3: Enhancing Food Quality and Safety

 

(a)       Enhancing food quality and safety standards, through, inter alia: (i) strengthening selected food quality and safety institutions’ capacities in disease and pests controls, traceability, inspections, risk assessment, as well as laboratory capacity and testing in food safety, veterinary and phytosanitary areas; (ii) alignment with the relevant EU legislation and international standards and requirements; (iii) investments into veterinary, inspection, food quality and safety infrastructure, including  procurement of necessary laboratory and IT equipment, as well as consumables, and Training.

 

(b)       Strengthening IT systems for food safety enhancement with the purpose of alignment and compliance with EU requirements, through, inter alia, development and upgrading of IT software and hardware systems in veterinary, food safety and plant health areas.

 

(c)       Review and upgrade of the veterinary IT systems, upgrade of the phytosanitary system, and of the food safety system for the benefit of MoFTER and FSA.

 

  1. Component 4: Project Management

This Component relates to coordination, administration, monitoring and evaluation of the Project.

 

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised November 2017 and August 2018) (Procurement Regulations), and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations. After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided a no objection.

 

Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement will be announced, as they become available, in UN Development Business online, on the World Bank’s external website and in leading local newspapers.

Interested eligible firms and individuals who would wish to be considered for the provision of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services for the above mentioned project, or those requiring additional information, should contact the Borrower at the address below:

The Government of the People's Republic of China has received a loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development to improve food safety management at the national and sub-national levels and to reduce food safety risks in selected value chains. The project is being implemented by the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, Guangdong Province, and Shandong Province (Yantai City).

As part of this project, this study proposes to conduct research on the AI-Based Digital Standardized Aquaculture Technology Model. This will continuously enhance quality and safety throughout the production process, ultimately establishing a standardized aquaculture system.

TOR for the Consulting Advisor's Work on Research of AI-Based Digital Standardized Aquaculture Technology Model (Contract No.: GDCS-020) under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

To facilitate the organization and implementation of the agricultural product quality and safety research under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project (hereinafter referred to as the "World Bank Loan Project"), and to ensure the successful completion of the project in accordance with its objectives and schedule, the Guangdong Center for Agricultural Product Quality and Safety (Guangdong Green Food Development Center) intends to hire a consulting advisor to conduct research on the AI-based digital standardized aquaculture technology model.

I.Background

As a vital component of China's agricultural economy, the aquaculture industry is a key sector for ensuring food security and optimizing dietary structures. With the continuous upgrading of consumer demands for aquatic product quality and increasingly stringent ecological and environmental protection policies, the traditional extensive aquaculture model can no longer meet the requirements of high-quality development. Particularly in terms of quality and safety supervision, aquaculture still faces prominent challenges, such as opaque production processes, delayed risk early warnings, and difficulties in tracing key indicators.

Due to its unique industrial characteristics, aquaculture still exhibits significant shortcomings in digital supervision practices. On the one hand, the dynamic and ever-changing aquatic environment involves multi-dimensional spatial interactions across the upper atmosphere, surface water bodies, and underwater ecosystems, making it difficult for traditional single monitoring methods to achieve full-scenario coverage. On the other hand, aquatic activities are characterized by concealment and suddenness. Traditional monitoring methods suffer from limited scope, untimely information acquisition, difficulty in identifying hidden behaviors, insufficient data accuracy, and high labor costs. These issues make the establishment of a standardized aquaculture system an urgent priority.

The core of this research lies in utilizing modern information technologies to achieve intelligent management of agricultural product quality and safety. Traditional production monitoring methods still face issues such as incomplete information collection and delayed responses to risk early warnings. To better address these challenges and further promote the digitalization of agricultural product quality and safety supervision, there is an urgent need to rely on modern information technologies—including AI, big data, IoT sensors, and cloud computing—to continuously improve the regulatory system. This is particularly crucial for process supervision and quality traceability in aquaculture, aiming to achieve full-chain safety management from production to distribution. This will not only help enhance the market competitiveness of agricultural products but also lay a solid foundation for the sustainable development of agricultural product quality and safety.

 

II.Objectives and Tasks

(I) Objectives

To address the current issues in aquaculture, including restricted information collection, delayed acquisition of key indicators, and the difficulty of tracing growth processes that lead to insufficient quality and safety, this project proposes to carry out the Development of an AI-Based Standardized Aquaculture System. Building upon existing development advantages and targeting the modernization of aquaculture, the project will dynamically monitor the growth status of aquatic products and implement timely interventions. This will continuously enhance product quality and safety throughout the production process, ultimately establishing a standardized aquaculture system.

(II) Specific Tasks

This research utilizes integrated space-air-ground intelligent technology, combined with remote sensing meteorological inversion, to accurately forecast key meteorological factors for the next 7 to 15 days, providing data support for large-scale cowpea planting management. By leveraging deep visual technology and crop growth prediction models, the study forecasts cowpea growth trends and establishes a pest and disease risk early-warning system. This enables precise fertilizer and pesticide application, promoting green and precision pest control. Furthermore, demonstration sites will be set up to host technical observation and training sessions, ultimately driving the safe, green, and sustainable development of cowpea production.

1.SWOT Analysis 

Summarize the current application status and existing challenges of new technologies, including satellite remote sensing, UAV remote sensing, ground sensors, and AI, in aquaculture production. Taking into account the actual conditions of the aquaculture production areas in the project pilot city, and considering multiple factors such as policy, economy, society, and technology, identify specific areas for investigation and evaluation. Examples include cost-benefit analysis, user acceptance surveys, and technical reliability testing. Meanwhile, ensure that the analysis provides a solid basis for subsequent strategy formulation.

2.Development of Intelligent Recognition Algorithms for Aquaculture Status Based on Low-Altitude Sensing Technology

Utilize drones to capture high-definition images or videos near automatic feeders. Combined with deep learning technology, accurately analyze aquatic product density, feeding behavior, health status, and pathological characteristics. The study will precisely extract the intrinsic correlations between image features and aquaculture status, effectively addressing the issues of untimely and imprecise perception in traditional monitoring methods. This will significantly enhance the timeliness and accuracy of aquaculture status monitoring, providing robust algorithmic support for the intelligent management of aquaculture.

3. Development of a Big Data-Driven Standardized Digital Aquaculture Management System

Integrate multi-source data to comprehensively analyze aquaculture growth processes, feeding records, and growth status early warnings, thereby achieving the digitalization of the aquaculture process. Meanwhile, based on time-series analysis and observation, monitor aquatic product quality in real-time and implement timely interventions to continuously provide quality and safety recommendations throughout the production process. Comprehensively map the complex relationships among the water environment, meteorological conditions, biological status, and aquaculture farming operations to establish a standardized digital aquaculture system. This will realize full-process digital and information-based management of aquaculture, thoroughly resolving industry pain points such as unsmooth information flow and untimely farming operations. Ultimately, it will ensure the quality and safety of aquatic products across the entire chain from source to terminal, driving the high-quality development of the aquaculture industry.

4.Exploration and Screening of New Technologies

Develop aquaculture status recognition algorithms that integrate remote sensing with low-altitude sensing. The remote sensing analysis will utilize drones to dynamically and automatically capture high-definition images or videos near automatic feeders. Combined with remote sensing technologies for aquaculture environment analysis, the system will accurately analyze aquatic product density, feeding behavior, health status, and pathological characteristics, thereby achieving refined aquaculture status recognition.

Screening Criteria: Focusing on core indicators such as technological maturity, cost-effectiveness, and environmental adaptability, the optimal technology portfolio will be determined through laboratory simulations and pilot validations.

5.Development of an Integrated "Space-Air-Ground-Water" Technical System

Hardware Layer: Deploy a satellite remote sensing monitoring network, UAV inspection systems, and IoT water quality sensors to achieve full-dimensional dynamic tracking and identification of aquatic product status and the environment in the production areas.

Platform Layer: Utilize an aquaculture big data cloud platform to integrate a multi-source data fusion engine, AI analysis modules (such as density recognition and disease prediction), and a visual decision-making dashboard, supporting synchronized access via both PC and mobile clients.

Application Layer: Implement an intelligent decision-making system. Based on inversion models and growth prediction algorithms, it will automatically generate agronomic recommendations such as feeding amounts and water replacement cycles, and push them to farmers via mobile apps or mini-programs.

6. Effectiveness Evaluation and Promotion & Application

Multi-dimensional Evaluation: Quantify evaluation indicators such as the water quality compliance rate and disease incidence rate. Select two typical aquaculture demonstration sites in the Pearl River Delta to conduct application demonstrations. Verify the technological effectiveness through comparative trials, thereby providing a complete technical solution for the Guangdong Aquatic Product Quality and Safety Enhancement initiative. This will strongly drive the digital transformation and high-quality development of the aquaculture industry, demonstrating robust competitiveness and development potential in the era of the digital economy.

Basic Requirements for Aquaculture Demonstration Bases: The pond aquaculture area must be no less than 200 mu. Bases must establish an agricultural product quality and safety management system in accordance with the law, produce in compliance with relevant agricultural product quality and safety standards, and maintain digitalized production records for agricultural products.

III.Qualification Requirements for the Consultant

1.Capability to independently bear civil liability (Must provide a copy of the Business License or the Certificate of Legal Person for Public Institutions);

2.Sound financial accounting system (Must provide audited financial reports for the past 3 years);

3.Possess the equipment and professional technical capabilities necessary for the performance of the contract (A commitment letter providing the supporting inspection drones and essential testing equipment [as specified in ] must be submitted);

4.Good record of tax and social security payment in accordance with the law (Must provide proof of tax payment and social security contribution for the past 3 months);

5.Good business credit and sound business performance (Must provide a statement certifying no major illegal or irregular business activities in the past 3 years, and that the applicant is not listed on the "Credit China" website as a "person subject to enforcement for dishonesty," "major tax violation entity," or "entity with serious illegal acts in government procurement").

6.Track Record: Within the past five years (from January 1, 2021, up to the deadline for submitting the Letter of Intent for this project, subject to the contract signing date), the Consultant shall have signed no less than one similar performance contract. A similar performance contract refers to a technical consulting service contract involving the application of drones, remote sensing imagery, or AI intelligent recognition in agricultural research, or a service contract for research on intelligent and standardized aquatic product production technology. The African Union has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Africa Centres for Disease Control Support Program to Combat Current and Future Public Health Threats Project. The Project Development Objective is to enhance the capacity of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) to support AU Member States in preventing, detecting, and responding to current and future public health threats and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

1. BACKGROUND

Health Information Systems interoperability is a foundational requirement for implementing national Health Information Exchange (HIE). A robust, standards-based interoperability framework is essential to enable secure data exchange, support system integration, and establish the technical and governance foundation for sustainable HIE implementation. Findings from the HIE maturity assessments conducted across AU Member States have identified interoperability as a high-impact priority, critical to enabling subsequent phases such as governance strengthening and phased digital health system implementation.

As part of the support by Africa CDC in implementing HIE across Member States, digital maturity assessments were conducted in 12 AU Member States, alongside the development of HIE roadmaps. Following this, Africa CDC will support two of countries, Tunisia and Seychelles, through the engagement of two individual consultants to support each of the countries to design and develop comprehensive interoperability frameworks aligned with international best practices and tailored to their national contexts.

2. OBJECTIVES

The purpose of this assignment is to design two country-specific, standards-based national interoperability frameworks that provide:

  • A structured architecture for health data exchange
  • Governance and institutional coordination mechanisms
  • Standards alignment and implementation guidance
  • A phased, actionable roadmap for national HIE implementation

3. SCOPE OF WORK

The consultants will provide technical leadership and advisory support to develop national interoperability framework as a foundational component of its Health Information Exchange (HIE). The consultants will conduct a structured review of the current digital health ecosystem, identify interoperability needs and gaps, and design a comprehensive framework aligned with internationally recognised best practices.

The scope of work includes:

  • Defining a layered interoperability model addressing technical, semantic, organisational, and legal dimensions,
  • Proposing standards-based data exchange approaches aligned with recognised international frameworks,
  • Developing high-level architecture principles to guide secure system integration,
  • Providing governance guidance to support institutional coordination and oversight,
  • Identifying security, privacy, and sustainability considerations,
  • Developing a phased implementation roadmap suitable for national adoption,
  • Developing an M&E framework.

The consultants will conduct consultations, technical discussions, document reviews, and validation sessions with designated counterparts. The assignment focuses on framework development and strategic planning; it does not include system procurement, software development, or direct implementation activities.

Specific institutional stakeholders and documentation to be reviewed will be provided by the Ministry of Health

Draft framework outlining architecture principles, governance guidance, standards alignment, security considerations, and interoperability layers

To present proposed national framework for technical and stakeholder review

Comprehensive technical framework document

By end of Month 4

Validation Workshop Materials and Revised Framework

Presentation materials and updated framework incorporating stakeholder input

To ensure national ownership and technical validation

Slide deck plus revised framework document

Month 5

Final Interoperability Framework and Implementation Roadmap

Finalized framework and phased implementation roadmap with recommendations and executive summary

To provide an actionable, endorsed national interoperability framework

Final report with roadmap and executive summary

End of Month 6

5. METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH EXPECTATIONS

The consultants are expected to apply internationally recognized best practices in digital health interoperability, drawing on established guidance and frameworks such as those promoted by global public health and standards organizations (for example WHO digital health guidance, HL7 interoperability standards, ISO principles for information systems, Open HIE architectural approaches, etc). The methodology should be consultative, evidence-based, and iterative, ensuring alignment with national priorities and feasibility within institutional capacities.

The approach should demonstrate clear consideration of security, privacy, scalability, governance alignment, and long-term sustainability. The consultants should ensure that recommendations are practical, actionable, and structured for phased implementation.

Consultants may exchange information among themselves to explore approaches, tools, strategies that may make their efforts more effective.

6. DURATION AND LEVEL OF EFFORT 

The assignment will be conducted over a maximum period of six months. The level of effort is expected to be full-time or near full-time engagement as required to complete deliverables within agreed timelines.

Specific start and end dates: Upon signing contract.

7. DUTY STATIONS

Duty station and modality: In country at the Ministry of Health of the respective countries (Tunisia and Seychelles)

8. REPORTING AND INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

The consultants will report technically to Director of Surveillance and Disease Intelligence at Africa CDC and the Ministry of Health-designated national counterparts. The consultants will work closely with relevant technical teams and stakeholders identified by the Ministry to ensure that the interoperability framework reflects national priorities and institutional realities.

The Consultants should have a strong understanding of the national digital health ecosystem. They will be based in-country and will regularly engage with key stakeholders through meetings and consultations. In addition, regular coordination meetings, technical discussions, and document review sessions will be held with Africa CDC and relevant national stakeholders to ensure alignment and steady progress.

Oversight and review mechanisms, including designated focal points, validation procedures, and formal approval processes, will be established at the start of the assignment. These arrangements will define communication channels, feedback timelines, and deliverable endorsement procedures to ensure accountability and quality assurance throughout the consultancy period.

Administrative coordination and contractual management will be handled by Africa CDC.

9. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The consultants must possess advanced expertise in digital health interoperability, health information systems architecture, or a closely related field. The consultants should demonstrate substantial experience designing interoperability frameworks, enterprise architectures, or national digital health strategies, preferably at national or multi-country level.

The consultant must meet the following requirements:

  • Advanced university degree in health informatics, information systems, computer science, public health, or related discipline,
  • Demonstrated experience developing interoperability frameworks or national health information system architectures,
  • Proven knowledge of global interoperability standards and frameworks,
  • Proven experience working with ministries, public agencies, or international organizations on comparable assignments.
  • Strong analytical and technical writing skills,
  • Fluency in English and French is mandatory for candidates applying to be selected to support Seychelles. Furthermore, fluency in Arabic is required for candidates applying to be selected to support Tunisia,
  • A minimum of ten (10) years of relevant experience is required in areas such as digital health interoperability, health information systems architecture, or national digital health strategy development.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of the preferred country’s health and digital health context, relevant institutions, governance arrangements, and stakeholder landscape, together with proficiency in the country’s applicable working language(s), sufficient to conduct consultations, review relevant documentation, and deliver the assignment effectively.

10. CORE COMPETENCIES

The consultant should demonstrate strong professional competencies including strategic thinking, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, communication skills, and the ability to translate complex technical concepts into practical guidance. The consultant must also show strong organizational skills, ability to meet deadlines, and capacity to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.

11. CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION, AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

The consultants shall adhere to the highest standards of professional integrity and confidentiality. All information, documents, data, and materials accessed during the assignment shall be treated as confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party without prior written authorisation.

The consultants shall comply with applicable data protection principles and institutional policies concerning the handling of sensitive or restricted information.

All reports, frameworks, tools, and materials developed under this assignment shall become the property of Africa CDC and the Ministry of Health. The consultants shall not use, reproduce, or distribute any deliverables or underlying materials for purposes unrelated to this assignment without prior written approval.

12. PAYMENT TERMS AND SCHEDULE

Consultancy fees are capped at $50,000 per consultant, totalling $100,000 for two consultants, with each consultant assigned to support one country. Payments will be made upon satisfactory completion and formal acceptance of agreed deliverables, based on a milestone schedule linked to the submission and approval of key outputs. Payments will be made based on satisfactory completion and formal acceptance of agreed deliverables. 13. CLARIFICATIONS, AMENDMENTS, AND COMMUNICATION PROTOCOL

All communications regarding this assignment shall be conducted through officially designated focal points identified at the start of the consultancy. Communication channels, reporting frequency, and feedback timelines will be formally agreed upon during the inception phase.

Any substantive modifications to the scope of work, deliverables, timeline, or level of effort must be agreed in writing by Africa CDC and the respective Ministry of Health. procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF ZAMBIA

MINISTRY OF GREEN ECONOMY AND ENVIRONMENT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Project: Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development (TRALARD) II Project

Grant/Project ID No.: P507971

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services to Align Private Cookstove Projects with the Jurisdictional ERP in Muchinga Province

Reference No.: ZM-MGEE-570653-CS-CQS

 

The Government of the Republic of Zambia, through the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment (MGEE), has received financing from the World Bank, the Climate Investment Funds (CIF), the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Least Developed Countries Fund (LDCF), the Nordic Development Fund and Scaling Climate Action by Lowering Emissions (SCALE), totalling USD 137 million, to support implementation of the Transforming Landscapes for Resilience and Development (TRALARD) II Project in Copperbelt, Luapula, Muchinga, Northern and Southern Provinces. The Government intends to apply part of the proceeds towards payments under the contract for the consulting services described below.

The objective of the assignment is to produce a technically robust, policy-aligned methodology and operational process that reconciles private cookstove project emission-reduction claims with jurisdictional emission-reduction accounting under the Muchinga ERP and Zambia’s national carbon-market framework, enabling continued project operations and transparent discounting where appropriate.

Scope of the Services

  • Prepare and validate the inception report, methodology, work plan and assignment launch arrangements.
  • Review the cookstove policy, legal and institutional framework for carbon-market regulation.
  • Inventory and technically assess active and pipeline cookstove projects in Muchinga Province.
  • Develop harmonized methodological rules for reconciling and discounting project-level emission reductions under the ERP.
  • Undertake technical assessments, sample recalculations and define MRV and registry interoperability requirements.

The Government of the People's Republic of China has received a loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development to improve food safety management at the national and sub-national levels and to reduce food safety risks in selected value chains. The project is being implemented by the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, Guangdong Province, and Shandong Province (Yantai City).

As part of this project, Guangdong Province plans to deepen the development of its agricultural product quality supervision system and leverage modern information technologies to achieve a smart management model for agricultural product quality and safety. Taking the characteristic lychee industry as a breakthrough, the province will carry out research on and application of new technologies for lychee agricultural safety. By utilizing cutting-edge information technologies such as drones, artificial intelligence, and big data, the project will collect, integrate, and analyze data on lychee growth and quality safety. This will enable precise identification of growth conditions, timely risk early warnings, and automated dispatch of agricultural practices throughout the entire lychee cultivation cycle.
